outcome.text: You earn eight gold for arranging an unusually exclusive alphabet. {{other}} calls the result historically inevitable.

title: THE AMNESTY WITH A PRICE BESIDE EACH NAME
text: {{other}} offers to submit names for a poaching amnesty. The list includes a fee column that the royal notice appears to have forgotten.

choices.label: Compare the terms with the public notice

outcome.text: The fee column disappears. {{other}} complains that copying the law word for word leaves no room for initiative.
You collect ten gold for exposing your neighbours to an arrangement you have not verified. {{other}} now has both the names and yours.

title: THE FIRST DRAFT IS STILL WET
text: {{other}} asks you to confirm a statement while the clerk has its contradictory first draft drying beside the fire.

outcome.text: The clerk keeps both copies. {{other}} is annoyed that your conscience has developed such inconvenient timing.

choices.label: Pay to destroy the first draft (7g)

outcome.text: The clerk takes your money and declines to burn evidence. You have purchased a very clear memory in somebody else’s head.

charge.offence: Attempting to destroy a witness statement

title: THE OAK HAS ARRIVED IN TWO OPINIONS
text: {{other}} delivers split timber for sound-timber money. The split is described as evidence that you can now see the quality inside.

choices.label: Reject the faulty lot and record why

outcome.text: The seller takes it back under witnesses. {{other}} finds a customer with less interest in the inside of wood.

choices.label: Buy cheaply and disclose the limits

outcome.text: You pay for usable offcuts, mark the defects and adapt the work. {{other}} is offended that the discount has become part of the description.

title: THE DRIVER RETURNS WITHOUT THE CART
text: {{other}} returns with no cart and an account containing a bridge, a lord and an extremely powerful pig. The freight receipt mentions none of them.

choices.label: Compare the route, witnesses and receipts

outcome.text: The story loses its lord, then its bridge. The pig survives as a regrettable error in loading, for which {{other}} accepts responsibility.
{{other}} pays eight gold and signs for the missing goods. The pig is left out of the agreement to save parchment.

title: THE CONTRACT UNDER THE SUPPER BOWL
text: {{other}} offers you private work while your fellow workers dispute the rate. The contract is concealed beneath a bowl, though the wage is not large enough to require hiding.

choices.label: Return the contract and explain why

outcome.text: {{other}} puts the bowl back with great dignity. Your fellow workers know you declined before the story could improve itself.
You receive nine gold. {{other}} can now quote your rate to everyone else, which proves much more valuable than the bowl.

title: THE ACCOUNT WITH TWO BURIALS FOR ONE MAN
text: {{other}} collects dues using a roll that has charged one household for the same burial twice. The second entry praises the deceased’s reliability.

outcome.text: The duplicate is struck out and the household keeps its payment. {{other}} announces that a dead clerk must have done it; no living clerk volunteers to disagree.

choices.label: Pay the disputed fee for the household (6g)

outcome.text: You cover the immediate demand and insist on a receipt. {{other}} now has to explain why the deceased has paid so promptly in person.

title: THE WITNESS HAS THREE NEW HENS
text: {{other}} offers testimony supporting a levy exemption. Their yard has three new hens and their memory has improved by exactly that many birds.

choices.label: Ask who paid for the hens

outcome.text: {{other}} withdraws the useful part of the statement and becomes indignant about your interest in poultry.
The testimony improves. The clerk records the payment as carefully as the evidence you hoped it would replace.

title: THE CHARTER IN THE FAMILY CHEST
text: {{other}} finds a charter fragment being used beneath a loose chest foot. It may establish a guild right; it certainly establishes why the chest used to wobble.

outcome.text: The copy preserves the right and the original goes somewhere dry. {{other}} repairs the chest with an ordinary piece of wood, now recognised as such.

choices.label: Sell exclusive access to the document

outcome.text: You pocket twelve gold. {{other}} learns how quickly a public right can become a private appointment.

title: THE LORD HAS BORROWED YOUR REPAIR TIMBER
text: {{other}} has moved your repair timber to the lord’s granary. The steward describes it as communal necessity, with a surprisingly precise sense of whose community you belong to.

choices.label: Quote the repair right before witnesses

outcome.text: The custom is real and the timber comes back. {{other}} complains that knowing the law has made you very difficult to govern efficiently.
Your roof is repaired and the granary keeps its timber. {{other}} calls this an excellent practical resolution, having paid for neither.

title: THE WALL THAT HID THE DAMP GRAIN
text: {{other}} opens a newly built partition and finds damp grain behind it. The mason says the wall had been intended to improve appearances.

choices.label: Sort and dry what can be saved

outcome.text: You lose a day’s strength and rescue useful stores. {{other}} agrees that food improves a household’s appearance best from inside its occupants.

choices.label: Sell the lot without mentioning the wall

outcome.text: You take twelve gold and lose household stores. {{other}} has retained a sack that illustrates your account rather well.

title: THE BOX THE FIRE DID NOT OPEN
text: {{other}} finds a locked strongbox in the burned rubble and asks whose it is. The owner’s mark is still readable, if inconveniently so.

outcome.text: The owner receives the box through {{other}}. Nobody has to invent a story about how the fire consumed the name but spared the lock.

choices.label: Force the lock and take the contents

outcome.text: You gain fourteen gold. {{other}} has seen the mark and now knows precisely how much your honesty costs.

charge.offence: Taking marked property from a fire

title: THE SCHOLAR’S VERY CAREFUL SILENCE
text: {{other}} has examined a supposed holy bone and offers an expensive explanation of why it would be unwise to explain the result.

outcome.text: The bone is an ordinary sheep’s. {{other}} is relieved until you ask for the answer in ordinary writing as well.
Your description mentions antiquity, dignity and almost everything except sheep. {{other}} makes sure not to sign the interesting part.

title: THE MOST ALIVE CORPSE
text: A draft claim lists {{parent}} as dead and asks for your household’s goods. {{parent}} arrives to dispute it. {{other}}, who supports the claim, asks whether the alleged deceased has brought a witness.

choices.label: Put your very audible parent before the witnesses

outcome.text: {{parent}} reads the claim aloud, adding objections in the margins. Your household keeps its goods; {{other}} acquires a personal reason to dislike you.
You pay nine gold to stop a living person being inventoried. {{parent}} refuses to call the payment a funeral expense.

choices.label: Support the false claim and take the offered share (fraud)

outcome.text: {{other}} pays your share. {{parent}} supplies the court with a living witness against you: {{parent}}.

title: THE FUNERAL REHEARSAL
text: {{parent}} wants to hear the funeral speech while corrections are still possible. The first objection is to the word “patient.”

outcome.text: {{parent}} disputes three dates and concedes one unkindness. You leave with a better account of the living person.
{{parent}} approves, then asks which parent you were describing. Affection survives the accusation.

title: THE INHERITANCE OF THREE KEYS
text: {{other}} offers to sell you three keys said to open a rich relative’s chest. The relative is less clearly identified than the price.

outcome.text: The smith identifies a stable key, a padlock key and an ambitious piece of wire. You pay for the inspection and keep your savings.
The keys open nothing you own. Fourteen gold has passed into a household with better working locks.

choices.label: Leave the chest to its remarkable relatives

outcome.text: You decline. {{other}} lowers the price so quickly that you feel richer without buying anything.

title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S NEW BAILIFF
text: {{child}} has begun charging visitors a toll of buttons. A visiting neighbour has paid in order to find out what happens next.

choices.label: Make the little collector restore every button

outcome.text: {{child}} returns the buttons under supervision. The household loses an afternoon and gains an accountant who now understands refunds.

choices.label: Declare the doorstep a lawful little manor

outcome.text: You defend the toll. The household’s standing falls, but {{child}} gains confidence in the hereditary nature of nonsense.

choices.label: Turn the whole levy into a counting lesson

outcome.text: You replace the toll with a game that gives the buttons back. {{child}} discovers that rules can be improved without conquering the neighbours.

title: THE BED IN THE WILL
text: {{sibling}} wants the better bed when your household divides its goods. The argument has reached the point of measuring old childhood injuries against the mattress.

choices.label: Trade the bed for a fair division of other goods

outcome.text: You surrender the bed and keep the dispute from becoming a family occupation. {{sibling}} thanks you without listing the injuries again.

choices.label: Offer to saw the bed exactly in half

outcome.text: {{sibling}} refuses the proposal and the relationship deteriorates. You keep the goods, together with the saw’s excellent negotiating reputation.

choices.label: Keep the goods together until there is actual need

outcome.text: The division waits. You use the intervening quiet to mend the bedding. It becomes easier to sleep on than the argument.

title: THE HEIR WITH THE WRONG FACE
text: {{parent}} commissions a little family portrait and asks that you be painted looking more like a prosperous relation. The painter has brought a ruler.

outcome.text: The portrait remains unpainted while you explain yourself. {{parent}} is disappointed, but no commission fee leaves the household.

choices.label: Pay for an honest portrait instead (8g)

outcome.text: The painter uses your actual nose. {{parent}} admits the nose belongs to the household. You accept the nearest available thing to praise.

title: THE PENSION PAID IN BREAD
text: {{parent}} insists that support should arrive as bread rather than promises. The loaf specified in the agreement is drawn at its desired size.

choices.label: Set aside stores for the support

outcome.text: You put food into the household reserve and reduce the ready coin available to you. {{parent}} approves the part that can be sliced.
{{parent}} asks whether the promise can be toasted. Trust declines, though the question improves the discussion.

choices.label: Repair the hearth instead of pledging money

outcome.text: The household’s living conditions improve. {{parent}} accepts work that can be felt through a cold evening.

title: YOUR NAME UNDER SOMEONE ELSE’S DEBT
text: {{sibling}} has promised a lender that you will guarantee a loan. Your signature looks splendid, particularly for something you did not write.

outcome.text: The lender cancels the claim. {{sibling}} offers to sign a note of gratitude; you suggest leaving the pen where it is.
The family’s reputation suffers under the accusation. You keep your purse and acquire a genuine sibling rivalry in place of a counterfeit signature.

choices.label: Accept the obligation, not the forgery

outcome.text: You record a real twenty-gold debt in your own name. {{sibling}} promises to remember it; the lender has a more dependable method.

title: THE COAT WITH ROOM TO GROW
text: {{child}} hates the new coat because it has room for another child inside. The tailor calls this economy; {{child}} calls it a tent.

choices.label: Pay for a coat that fits this year (4g)

outcome.text: The sleeves stop collecting soup. {{child}} is delighted by the expensive discovery of wrists.

choices.label: Teach a fold that makes the sleeves useful

outcome.text: You fold, stitch and let {{child}} choose the thread. The household gains a small practical skill and a less furious wearer.

title: THE LADDER THAT IS NEVER HOME
text: {{other}} has borrowed your household’s ladder so often that visitors now ask directions to it rather than to you.

choices.label: Retrieve it and help finish the repair

outcome.text: You bring the ladder home after helping with the roof. {{other}} owes you a kindness, and the household can reach its own rafters again.
{{other}} pays five gold and becomes much less neighbourly. The ladder has earned more than most apprentices.

choices.label: Give it away and make a lower set of shelves

outcome.text: {{other}} takes the ladder home permanently. You lower the shelves and stop receiving requests to borrow your furniture’s only means of escape.

title: THE SALT CELLAR’S SECOND BOTTOM
text: {{parent}} shows you the household’s hidden savings beneath the salt. The ceremony would feel grander if the emergency reserve did not smell of herring.

choices.label: Leave the reserve where it is

outcome.text: You promise discretion. {{parent}} trusts you with something more substantial than a story.

choices.label: Take twelve gold from the household reserve

outcome.text: The household loses twelve gold and you gain it. {{parent}} discovers the missing weight before the missing salt.
The reserve grows. {{parent}} moves you from the category of people protected by it to the category of people protecting it.

title: THE CONDITIONAL BLESSING
text: {{child}} has written a promise to obey you “where reasonably convenient.” It has been copied beautifully.

outcome.text: You agree on chores and limits. {{child}} keeps the phrase in the copy, now accompanied by a rather demanding definition.
You enforce obedience and damage trust. {{child}} learns to leave a wider margin for thoughts you will not read.

title: THE ROOF’S CONTRIBUTION TO SUPPER
text: Rain falls onto your household’s table. {{other}} offers a hurried roof repair, priced on the assumption that you have already noticed the weather.

outcome.text: The bowls return to holding supper instead of rain. The repairer leaves with your money and, at last, the household’s weather.

choices.label: Patch it together and lose a day’s rest

outcome.text: The patch improves the roof modestly. Your back protests a job that the clouds had made urgent.

choices.label: Spend nothing and let the room deteriorate

outcome.text: You move the bowls and keep the coin. The damp eats part of the stores without once presenting an estimate.

title: THE STOLEN FAMILY ANECDOTE
text: {{sibling}} tells your most embarrassing childhood story and gives themselves your heroic part. You are left with the bucket.

outcome.text: You correct the story in front of everyone. {{sibling}} loses affection for you; your family’s standing survives its inability to agree about a bucket.

choices.label: Tell the part where both of you fell in

outcome.text: You trade a little dignity for a better laugh. {{sibling}} remembers why the original story was worth keeping.

title: THE HONEST LITTLE WITNESS
text: {{child}} saw you conceal goods during an argument over a levy. The child is now asking whether lying becomes lawful at a particular age.

choices.label: Return the goods and admit the example was poor

outcome.text: You return the goods and pay the loss. {{child}} watches you admit the lesson before asking whether adults have to practise it too.
{{child}} stops asking and loses trust in you. A household secret is created, together with a witness who has reasons to resent it.
You abandon concealment and put your objection in public. Your family’s reputation improves without settling the assessment for the court.

title: THE LAST HILL ON THE ROAD
text: {{parent}} insists the road is no steeper than it used to be. Only the pauses have grown longer.

choices.label: Take the road at your parent’s pace

outcome.text: You lose the afternoon and keep the company. {{parent}} lets you carry the basket without calling it help.

choices.label: Hire a cart for the journey (5g)

outcome.text: {{parent}} complains about the expense all the way home. The complaint is delivered from a comfortable seat.

choices.label: Leave the basket and hurry ahead

outcome.text: You preserve your time and damage your parent’s trust. The rest of the road is quieter than you expected.

title: THE HEIRLOOMS ON THE MARKET CLOTH
text: {{sibling}} is selling household keepsakes to meet a creditor. Each object comes with a family story. The buyers ask for shorter stories and lower prices.

choices.label: Buy the goods back for the household (20g)

outcome.text: You pay for the keepsakes and put them back in the household. {{sibling}} thanks you for saving the objects without making a speech over each one.
You accept that survival can require parting with things. The family’s standing improves and {{sibling}} trusts you more.

choices.label: Buy cheaply and keep the proceeds yourself

outcome.text: You profit from the sale while the household loses wealth. {{sibling}} recognises exactly which family tradition you have preserved.

title: THE FAMILY SEAL CUT IN SOAP
text: {{sibling}} has cut a convincing family seal in soap. It is clever, cheap and already on an agreement nobody authorised.

choices.label: Destroy the seal and pay to correct the agreement (10g)

outcome.text: The false seal dissolves in a basin. Ten gold pays for correction, and {{sibling}} discovers an expensive use for clean hands.

choices.label: Use the false seal to obtain an advance

outcome.text: You receive the advance and create a genuine forgery charge. The soap has left a wonderfully clear impression on the evidence.

charge.offence: Obtaining an advance with a false seal

choices.label: Give the impression to the clerk

outcome.text: You expose the scheme and damage your bond with {{sibling}}. The household’s reputation suffers, but your own legal record remains clear.

title: THE BOWL KEPT WARM
text: {{child}} has kept a bowl beside the hearth for you. It is nearly cold; the child has been watching it for a long time.

outcome.text: You eat slowly enough to hear the whole account of the day. {{child}} stops watching the bowl.

choices.label: Thank the child while attending to other work

outcome.text: Your thanks is sincere and your attention is elsewhere. {{child}} learns the difference.

title: THE BOUNDARY MARK UNDER THE BED
text: {{sibling}} has brought a boundary stone indoors for safekeeping. Unfortunately it was keeping two households from arguing about the field.

outcome.text: The boundary is restored under witnesses rather than by memory. {{sibling}} helps carry it and resents the audience.

choices.label: Use the confusion to enlarge your household’s claim

outcome.text: Your household gains wealth from the disputed use, and you acquire a fraud charge. The stone is silent; the witnesses are not.
You fund a new survey and improve the household’s standing. {{sibling}} is disappointed that measuring settles what shouting could not.

title: THE WEDDING OF THREE GROOMS
text: {{sibling}} has promised to pay three different wedding brokers for one match. All three bring contracts to the same supper. The prospective marriage is the only part nobody has arranged.

outcome.text: You expose the conflicting promises. Family standing suffers and {{sibling}} blames the only person at supper who could read.

choices.label: Pay the brokers to cancel the claims (15g)

outcome.text: The contracts are cancelled for fifteen gold. Everybody leaves unmarried. The family counts this as the evening’s first clear success.

choices.label: Demand a share of the household’s wedding reserve

outcome.text: You take ten gold from the reserve. {{sibling}} now has three brokers and one blackmailer to satisfy.

title: THE INVENTORY OF MATRIMONY
text: {{spouse}} has drawn up a list of everything each of you brought to the marriage. Under your name, “confidence” is underlined twice.

choices.label: Add a fair account of the unpaid work

outcome.text: You list the work both of you do. {{spouse}} puts the inventory away before it needs another sheet.
You win the valuation and lose affection. {{spouse}} asks whether you would like a receipt for the triumph.

choices.label: Seek a formal separation and divide your goods

outcome.text: You end the marriage and surrender part of the household reserve. The list becomes useful in a way neither of you intended.

title: THE BENCH BETWEEN TWO FAMILIES
text: At your wedding anniversary meal, {{spouse}} objects to the order of the benches. Everyone insists that seating means nothing while refusing to move.

choices.label: Mix the benches and serve the food yourself

outcome.text: You put conversation before precedence. {{spouse}} helps, and the household’s reputation improves without buying another bench.

choices.label: Let your spouse choose the seats

outcome.text: {{spouse}} gets the arrangement right to at least one person’s satisfaction. Your willingness to yield is remembered kindly at home.

title: THE LOVE LETTER WITH A TALLY
text: {{other}} sends a declaration of affection on the back of a household account. The account is paid. This is the most encouraging part of the letter.

choices.label: Answer honestly, without promising a wedding

outcome.text: You begin a warmer acquaintance with {{other}}. Nobody is married by correspondence, though both of you enjoy the ink.
You and {{other}} marry by mutual consent. The household account becomes the least interesting part of the document.
You decline without circulating the letter. {{other}} appreciates having one disappointment instead of an audience.

title: THE PETITION AGAINST YOUR EVENINGS
text: {{spouse}} asks why every errand takes you past the same doorway. You offer a well-prepared explanation. {{spouse}} asks how long you have been preparing it.

choices.label: Give a full account and change the arrangement

outcome.text: You answer the question and make room for your spouse’s worry. Trust improves through a less entertaining use of the evening.

choices.label: Turn the suspicion into a public joke

outcome.text: The joke reaches an audience. {{spouse}} withdraws affection and acquires a grievance that is entirely about what you actually did.

choices.label: End the marriage rather than answer

outcome.text: You choose separation. The marriage ends, the household loses resources and the unanswered question survives without a husband or wife to ask it.

title: A SUITOR’S EARLY TESTAMENT
text: {{other}} offers you a marriage contract and a draft will in the same sitting. The second document has been written considerably more neatly.

choices.label: Discuss how to live together before discussing death

outcome.text: You leave the contracts unsigned and the acquaintance more honest. {{other}} is relieved to put away the better pen.

choices.label: Accept the marriage without the speculative will

outcome.text: You marry {{other}} by consent. Neither of you gains an inheritance in advance of anyone’s death.

choices.label: Forge a richer settlement than you own

outcome.text: You create a false marriage settlement without making a marriage. {{other}} becomes a witness to the fraud, not your spouse.

title: THE GIFT RETURNED IN BETTER WRAPPING
text: {{other}} returns a courtship gift wrapped more beautifully than when it left you. The rejection appears to have received professional help.

choices.label: Accept the answer and admire the wrapping

outcome.text: You take the refusal without turning it into a quarrel. {{other}} trusts you more for the boundary you respect.
You make an enemy of someone who had merely declined you. The wrapping is now the kindest part of the exchange.

title: A WITNESS TO THE WRONG ROMANCE
text: {{other}} asks you to swear you saw a courting couple promise marriage. You saw two people quarrel over a borrowed cloak, but the fee for remembering otherwise is tempting.

outcome.text: {{other}} folds the proposed testimony. Your memory has failed to become useful, an imperfection they find very difficult to forgive.

choices.label: Sign the false testimony for a promised reward

outcome.text: The clerk records your oath and asks a second question. {{other}} remembers promising payment rather less clearly than you remember promising to have been there.

choices.label: Warn the people whose names are being used

outcome.text: You publicly challenge the scheme. Your reputation rises while {{other}} acquires a specific grievance against you.

title: THE PRACTICAL LOVE POEM
text: {{spouse}} discovers a poem you wrote early in the marriage. Your present skill at remembering where the firewood is stored compares poorly with your former devotion.

choices.label: Fetch the wood before discussing the poem

outcome.text: The room warms and {{spouse}} accepts the new verse as an improvement. It has fewer adjectives and better fuel.
You make {{spouse}} laugh, though the wood remains where it was. Affection improves more than the room temperature.

title: THE IDENTICAL TOKEN
text: {{spouse}} finds a love token that looks exactly like one given to a neighbour. The pedlar who sold them is wisely absent.

choices.label: Admit the token came from a crowded stall

outcome.text: You admit that the token was common and the affection was not. {{spouse}} accepts the distinction after enjoying your discomfort.
Seven gold buys a token with a private inscription. {{spouse}} reads it twice before deciding not to ask what the first one cost.

choices.label: Accuse your spouse of inventing the comparison

outcome.text: You answer a small doubt with a larger cruelty. Trust falls, and the cheap token has become an expensive object.

title: THE PRICE OF PARTING
text: You and {{spouse}} are considering separation. The clerk has quoted for three copies: one for each of you and one for everyone who will pretend not to have read it.

outcome.text: The marriage ends and twelve gold pays for the record. The clerk is the only person who calls the day satisfactory.

choices.label: Try an honest conversation before signing

outcome.text: You keep the marriage and rebuild a little trust. It is a beginning, not a miraculous repair.

choices.label: Destroy the draft and forbid further discussion

outcome.text: The marriage continues under less trust. A torn document is easier to silence than the person who asked for it.

title: THE DOWRY WHICH HONKS
text: {{spouse}} wants the household’s wedding reserve spent on food rather than another display of respectability. The proposed display has a ribbon budget larger than its supper budget.

choices.label: Put the money into household food (9g)

outcome.text: You fund the reserve and cancel the ribbons. {{spouse}} values an anniversary that can be eaten.

choices.label: Buy the display and leave supper thin (9g)

outcome.text: The ribbons are splendid and the household’s food reserve shrinks. {{spouse}} declines to be nourished by colour.

choices.label: Hold a quiet meal with what you have

outcome.text: You choose an unshowy supper and keep your savings. {{spouse}} enjoys not having to praise anything you have bought.

title: THE CHAPERONE’S EXPENSES
text: {{other}} brings an itemised account for supervising two people’s courtship. “Looking away at suitable moments” is the largest charge.

choices.label: Ask the supervised couple to review the account

outcome.text: You expose the exaggerated bill without inventing a romantic scandal. {{other}} dislikes the new interest in arithmetic.

choices.label: Pay to spare the couple an argument (5g)

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts payment for having seen less. The bill is exceptionally legible for work conducted in such poor light.

title: THE SERENADE AT THE STOREROOM
text: {{other}} has been singing beneath a shutter that opens onto a storeroom. The household wants the flour left out of the next verse.

outcome.text: You save {{other}} from a second performance and gain a grateful acquaintance. The flour remains unmoved.
{{other}} discovers the error in public. Your reputation for wit rises slightly; your reputation with the singer falls considerably.

choices.label: Offer the singer a quiet cup indoors (3g)

outcome.text: You pay for a dry place to wait and close the door on the audience. {{other}} discovers that a little hospitality travels farther than the verse.

title: THE GUEST WHO CAME WITH THE MARRIAGE
text: {{spouse}} has invited a relation to stay. “A short visit” has now acquired a spare blanket and an opinion about the way you cook.

choices.label: Agree on a leaving date together

outcome.text: You and {{spouse}} settle the invitation without a public quarrel. Household trust improves and the spare blanket remains only a blanket.
The food is bought before the visit becomes an argument. {{spouse}} welcomes a contribution that has not brought its own speech.

choices.label: Order the guest out and blame your spouse

outcome.text: The household loses harmony and {{spouse}} loses trust in you. Winning the doorway has cost you something farther inside.

title: THE MATCHMAKER’S UNHELPFUL RECOMMENDATION
text: {{other}} recommends you for a marriage by praising your ability to withstand disappointment. You would prefer the compliment not to need so many examples.

choices.label: Set out what you actually want in a match

outcome.text: You replace a flattering description with an honest one. {{other}} understands you better and has less material for the next introduction.
Your invented position becomes a concealed falsehood. {{other}} is impressed by facts that will be expensive to defend.

title: THE ANNIVERSARY NEITHER MENTIONED
text: You and {{spouse}} have both forgotten the date of your marriage. Each of you is carefully waiting to see whether the other has remembered.

choices.label: Admit it first and share the relief

outcome.text: {{spouse}} laughs with the relief of a person acquitted before accusation. You begin a better evening than either of you had planned.

choices.label: Wait, then accuse your spouse of forgetting

outcome.text: You win a small advantage and spend it immediately on an argument. {{spouse}} is less inclined to celebrate the next year.

title: THE OATH THAT WAS NOT YOURS
text: {{other}} has circulated a claim that you promised marriage. You remember promising to return a borrowed pot. The pot is still at home.

outcome.text: You return the object you actually promised and reject the other claim publicly. {{other}} resents the clarity.
Nine gold buys an end to this claim, together with a secret about how readily your name can be priced.
Your counterclaim reaches the clerk, who recognises the false seal. You face a forgery charge; the pot has become the most innocent participant.

charge.offence: Forging evidence in a marriage dispute

title: THE LORD WHO TAXED SHADE
text: {{other}} demands rent because your roof casts a shadow over a boundary. A servant has measured the offence at noon, when it is cheapest.

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts seven gold for the shade. A cloud passes over the transaction without paying anything.

choices.label: Ask for a hearing with the measuring stick present

outcome.text: You bring the demand into public view. Your reputation rises and {{other}} becomes a named rival rather than an invisible expense.
The Commons gain confidence and {{other}}’s household records a feud with yours. Shade has become a matter of family honour.

familyFeud.reason: Opposed the demand for shadow rent

outcome.text: Four gold makes the measurements difficult to find. A secret remains about the smaller, more useful payment.

title: THE WINDOW WITH A FEE
text: In your cell, daylight comes through a gap {{other}} says can be widened. The price is clear. The size of the wall beyond it is less so.

choices.label: Keep your money and mend the bedding

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned and make the cell marginally less miserable. {{other}} loses interest in your purse.

choices.label: Attempt the escape (risk a severe head injury)

success.text: You squeeze through and reach open ground. You are outside the prison, with an outstanding charge and very little dignity.

failure.text: The opening leads to a fall. You remain imprisoned with a head injury, and the wall proves much firmer than the offer.

choices.label: Tell the gaoler about the proposed opening

outcome.text: You remain inside, but your cooperation improves your reputation. {{other}} will not offer you another window.

title: THE PARDON WITH ROOM FOR A NAME
text: {{other}} offers a blank royal pardon, complete with a convincing stain where the seal ought to be. It forgives anything you are prepared to write small enough.

outcome.text: You decline the forgery. {{other}} moves on to people who have more to forgive and less to lose.
You acquire a fresh forgery charge without erasing any older one. The stain receives considerably more official attention than expected.

choices.label: Give the blank to the clerk as evidence

outcome.text: You expose the scheme and gain standing with the Crown. {{other}} knows exactly who supplied the paper.

title: THE THIEF WHO STOLE THE SIGN
text: {{other}} has stolen a tradesperson’s sign rather than any goods. Customers are now queuing outside the thief’s empty shed.

choices.label: Help return the sign before opening time

outcome.text: You restore the sign and gain local standing. {{other}} calls this a waste of an unusually successful theft.

choices.label: Sell directions to the wrong shop (risk a fraud complaint)

success.text: You collect a small payment before the joke is discovered. The shed remains empty and you keep a secret about the route you sold.

failure.text: A customer follows the directions with you still in sight. The complaint names both the empty shed and the person selling its address.

charge.offence: Taking payment for a false shop

title: THE JUROR’S LUNCH
text: {{other}} asks you to carry a handsome pie to a juror. Inside the lid is the verdict the sender would prefer him to reach.

choices.label: Deliver the whole thing as evidence

outcome.text: You expose the attempted bribe and gain public standing. {{other}} regards the crust as a betrayal.
The delivery makes you a party to attempted bribery. The pie is consumed; the written suggestion is kept.

charge.offence: Carrying a bribe to a juror

choices.label: Return it unopened to its owner

outcome.text: You decline the errand and lose a little favour with {{other}}. Your supper remains your own responsibility.

title: THE PAID SUBSTITUTE
text: {{other}} offers a purse if you will stand in for a relative’s punishment. The promised mark on your arm is described as small by someone who will not be wearing it.

choices.label: Refuse a punishment that is not yours

outcome.text: {{other}} improves the offer, apparently believing your skin has failed to understand the first price. Your arm leaves the negotiation unchanged.

choices.label: Accept the money and the lasting injury

outcome.text: You receive twenty-four gold and a painful burn that leaves chronic pain. {{other}} is satisfied that the family punishment has been properly outsourced.
The public accusation damages {{other}}’s trust in you and improves your own standing. No part of the payment reaches your skin.

title: THE CLEANEST EVIDENCE
text: {{other}} wants a disputed receipt washed until the inconvenient line vanishes. The laundress has asked whether justice should be boiled with the linens.

choices.label: Keep the receipt dry and legible

outcome.text: The stain stays on the cloth and out of the wash. {{other}} calls this an unreasonable use of cleanliness as evidence.

choices.label: Wash away the line (risk an evidence charge)

success.text: The line vanishes before another copy can be compared. You keep the secret and gain {{other}}’s trust in your willingness to cross a boundary.

failure.text: A retained copy exposes the missing line. You acquire an evidence-destruction charge; the paper is cleaner than the account of washing it.

choices.label: Pay for witnessed copies before washing (3g)

outcome.text: You fund copies and make the original trick useless. {{other}} has to dispute what the document says instead of whether anyone can read it.

title: THE PRISON SUPPER LIST
text: Your cell’s meal list includes meat for four people. {{other}} asks whether anybody has seen either the meat or the other three.

choices.label: Add your name to a truthful complaint

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned and gain a little public standing for the complaint. {{other}} becomes a firmer ally inside the walls.
You buy food to share instead of waiting for the list to become edible. You recover some health and {{other}} trusts the meal more than the list.

choices.label: Save your own portion and refuse the argument

outcome.text: You eat your share in full. {{other}} watches the bowl empty with an expression that will be present at the next division.

title: THE ALIBI WITH A HOLE IN IT
text: {{other}} wants you to swear you spent the night together. The proposed alibi includes an hour when the whole square saw you somewhere else.

outcome.text: {{other}} asks whether you are quite certain you remember correctly. You remain inconveniently certain.

choices.label: Swear to the impossible evening (risk perjury)

success.text: The contradiction is not tested at this hearing. {{other}} gains trust in you and you acquire a secret whose witnesses still live in the square.

failure.text: The missing hour is put to witnesses. You acquire a perjury charge with unusually easy evidence.

title: THE ROPE INSPECTOR
text: {{other}} asks you to test a condemned climbing rope before it is sold again. The test consists of trusting the seller’s statement that it was only condemned on a technicality.

choices.label: Cut the rope so it cannot be sold

outcome.text: You destroy a dangerous bargain and gain public trust. {{other}} loses faith in your respect for private property.

choices.label: Test it above the quarry (risk a fatal fall)

success.text: The rope holds long enough for you to come down. You are paid ten gold and acquire an enduring dislike of technicalities.

failure.text: The condemned section parts over the quarry. The last assurance you hear is that it held yesterday.

effects.death: Killed in a fall while testing a condemned rope.

choices.label: Leave the seller without endorsing the rope

outcome.text: You decline to give an opinion that somebody might later mistake for a guarantee. {{other}} will need a different signature.

title: THE CHICKENS UNDER GUARD
text: {{other}} supports a new fine for wandering hens. The guard hired to watch the impounded birds is a dog, and expenses are rising whenever it looks hungry.

outcome.text: You make the claim difficult to defend and gain standing with the Commons. {{other}} becomes a rival with a remarkably poultry-shaped grievance.

choices.label: Contribute to the households’ release fund (6g)

outcome.text: You contribute to the relief fund. Your family’s reputation improves; the dog remains the only participant without a receipt.

choices.label: Claim the release money with forged ownership papers

outcome.text: You obtain eleven gold and a fraud charge. Several actual owners are able to identify what you do not own.

charge.offence: Claiming impounded birds with false papers

title: THE KEY THAT OPENS EVERY DOOR
text: {{other}} claims to have a prison key that opens every door. It is drawn on parchment. The proposed escape requires a smith and a great deal of belief.

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned without adding another charge to your record. {{other}} calls you unadventurous from inside a locked room.

choices.label: Commission the key and attempt escape (10g; more prison if caught)

success.text: The copied key opens a service door. You escape the cell, but remain wanted for breaking custody.

failure.text: The key turns in nothing. The search finds the drawing and adds three years to your sentence.

choices.label: Surrender the plan without accusing anyone else

outcome.text: The gaoler takes the plan and examines the drawing. {{other}} now regards you as a rival; the drawing has still opened more conversation than doors.

title: THE WITNESS IN A DIFFERENT CAP
text: {{other}} offers to testify twice in a boundary dispute using a different cap for the second appearance. The caps are convincing. The beard is exactly the same.

outcome.text: You expose the trick and improve your standing. {{other}} cannot decide which cap to wear while resenting you.

choices.label: Act surprised at the second witness (risk a charge)

success.text: You sustain the performance long enough to escape immediate questioning. {{other}} trusts you more, and the deception remains a dangerous secret.

failure.text: The beard is recognised between the two caps. You acquire a false-testimony charge for pretending not to notice it.

title: THE THIEF’S CONFESSION BOOK
text: {{other}} has stolen the book in which a penitent listed stolen goods. It may be the only theft in the lane that comes with its own inventory.

choices.label: Return the book without reading it aloud

outcome.text: You protect the private confession and improve your reputation. {{other}} sees the book depart without any of the profit intended for it.

choices.label: Use the list to demand money

outcome.text: You create a blackmail charge and a secret about your own conduct. Confession has finally added something to the list.

choices.label: Hand it to the clerk as evidence of the theft

outcome.text: You expose the theft and anger {{other}}. The book is treated as evidence rather than as an invitation to collect from everyone in it.

title: THE FINE FOR BEING AVAILABLE
text: A clerk has put your name on an unpaid fine because you were standing nearest the desk. {{other}} offers to vouch for you, provided you explain what innocence usually pays.

choices.label: Request the original charge and witnesses

outcome.text: You contest the clerical shortcut and gain local standing. {{other}} is disappointed to discover that assistance can be made unnecessary.

choices.label: Pay five gold and keep your day (5g)

outcome.text: The disputed fine is paid and a receipt supplied. {{other}} has settled the amount without once managing to establish the offence.

choices.label: Alter the account to name a neighbour

outcome.text: You create an actual forgery charge while trying to escape an administrative error. The clerk now has something definite to write.

title: THE COFFIN WHICH RATTLES
text: {{other}} offers work carrying a coffin that rattles like tableware. The supposed mourner asks you not to tilt his uncle.

choices.label: Ask to see the contents before agreeing

outcome.text: You ask to inspect the contents. {{other}} withdraws both the offer and the claim that curiosity is a virtue.

choices.label: Carry it past the toll (risk a smuggling charge)

success.text: You carry the contraband through and earn thirteen gold. {{other}} is grateful that you mourned at a steady walking pace.

failure.text: A lid slips and the customs men discover the uncle’s astonishing collection of spoons. A smuggling charge is entered against you.

charge.offence: Carrying concealed goods past a toll

choices.label: Leave the uncle to his own household

outcome.text: You decline before taking the load. Whatever is in the coffin will have to find someone else to be late for it.

title: THE APOLOGY SOLD BY THE LINE
text: {{other}} offers to draft an apology for your past misdeeds. Every admission costs extra, and the most expensive one is true.

outcome.text: You take responsibility without buying eloquence. Public reputation improves a little and the existing charges remain for the court to decide.
The clerk produces a statement worth reading. {{other}} looks relieved until you insist on reading the useful part aloud too.
You add a threat to the conduct that needed an apology. {{other}} becomes a rival with a useful memory.

title: THE NAME THAT BUYS A CELL
text: {{other}} claims that naming an accomplice will improve your conditions. The requested name belongs to someone you have no evidence against.

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned and keep your own testimony honest. {{other}} loses interest in your memory.
The clerk adds your false statement to the file. {{other}} has supplied an entirely genuine reason for both of you to be questioned again.

choices.label: Pay for a petition about your actual conditions (5g)

outcome.text: Your petition is lodged and receipted. {{other}} agrees that paper travels remarkably well through a door neither of you can open.

title: THE LIE EVERYONE PRACTISED
text: {{other}} rehearses a witness’s story so thoroughly that you are asked to supply the correct pause before the false accusation.

choices.label: Refuse to become the rehearsal’s witness

outcome.text: You reject the falsehood and gain a reputation for independence. {{other}} loses trust in you as an accomplice.

choices.label: Give the rehearsed accusation under oath (prison)

outcome.text: The contradiction is exposed and you are imprisoned for perjury. The court finds your perfectly timed hesitation especially persuasive evidence.

choices.label: Expose the rehearsal before testimony begins

outcome.text: You expose the scheme and acquire a named rival. {{other}} will have to rehearse a different explanation.

title: THE CONSTABLE’S SINGLE BOOT
text: {{other}} has found a constable’s boot with a purse inside. The missing constable is calling the theft an assault on authority; the boot looks undamaged.

choices.label: Return the boot and its contents

outcome.text: You return the find and improve your reputation. Authority is restored to a matching pair.

choices.label: Keep the purse and leave the boot (risk a theft charge)

success.text: You keep the purse’s contents and leave the boot where it will be found. {{other}} knows enough to make the money less comfortable than it feels.

failure.text: The constable finds the emptied boot before you have left the lane. The resulting theft charge includes an unusually recognisable piece of evidence.

charge.offence: Keeping the contents of a constable’s stolen boot

title: THE BARREL WITH A SECOND FLOOR
text: {{other}} wants your mark on barrels that hold less than their stated measure. The false bottoms fit beautifully. Honesty is the only badly made part.

choices.label: Keep your mark off the barrels

outcome.text: Your standing in the guild improves when you refuse. {{other}} looks for a craftsman whose signature is more flexible than the wood.

choices.label: Sign them and accept the fraudulent commission

outcome.text: You earn sixteen gold and create a fraud charge. The barrels’ workmanship is much easier to defend than your mark.

choices.label: Rework them into honestly sized vessels

outcome.text: The extra labour hurts your performance this year but earns experience and public standing. You have finally made something smaller without cheating.

title: THE CUSTOMER’S ROYAL ELL
text: {{other}} measures your finished work with an “ancient royal ell” that gets longer at the expensive end of the job.

choices.label: Bring the guild’s measure before discussing payment

outcome.text: You defend the agreed measure and gain guild standing. {{other}} loses confidence in the profitability of ancient custom.

choices.label: Do the extra work to keep the peace

outcome.text: You absorb the extra labour and gain a more grateful customer. Your performance suffers under the time it takes.

title: THE LEFT-HANDED APPRENTICE
text: {{other}} says an apprentice’s work is wrong because the tool is held in the wrong hand. The joint fits perfectly. This is becoming an awkward fact.

choices.label: Judge the work by the joint

outcome.text: You defend useful skill and improve your standing. {{other}} is less pleased to discover that custom can be tested against a table.
You enforce the rule, lose experience you might have gained and damage your reputation for fair judgement. The joint remains correct.

choices.label: Ask to be taught the method

outcome.text: You put down the rulebook and try the joint. {{other}} has the kindness not to mention how long the rulebook delayed this discovery.

title: THE MASTER’S MARK ON RUBBISH
text: {{other}} has found your mark on rejected goods. You can deny it, correct it or admit that someone has been selling what you were paid to discard.

choices.label: Recall the marked goods at your own expense (18g)

outcome.text: You fund the correction and preserve your post. Guild standing suffers less than your purse, and {{other}} accepts the repair.

choices.label: Deny the mark despite the matching die

outcome.text: The deception costs you your employment and a fraud charge is entered. The die continues to recognise its own work.

charge.offence: Selling rejected goods under a master’s mark

choices.label: Admit the breach and surrender the post

outcome.text: You leave the employment and lose guild standing. The admission avoids a new fabricated defence, not the consequences of the original breach.

title: THE DRY GOODS IN THE RIVER
text: {{other}} proposes a shipping venture described as dry goods. The proposed barge has no cover and the sky has supplied a rebuttal.

choices.label: Delay the venture and lose the small booking fee (3g)

outcome.text: The booking fee is lost; the goods remain dry. {{other}} begins to respect your caution at exactly the rate the rain increases.

choices.label: Borrow to fund the shipment (risk debt and household loss)

success.text: The goods arrive before the storm. The return reaches your purse, while the full loan remains a real debt to repay.

failure.text: The shipment fails. Your thirty-gold loan survives it, and the household loses wealth meeting the immediate costs.

choices.label: Pay for cover before committing a small stake (9g)

outcome.text: The covering is paid for and the terms recorded. {{other}} finds a contract rather less responsive to the weather than a promise.

title: THE SILENT PARTNER’S SPEECH
text: {{other}} proposes a silent partnership and spends an hour explaining how loudly you should defend it to creditors.

choices.label: Demand written limits to your liability

outcome.text: {{other}} reads the limits on “silent” twice. The second reading is noticeably quieter.

choices.label: Guarantee the debt to secure the partnership

outcome.text: You record a twenty-two-gold obligation and gain a more trusting partner. Trust is cheap to offer when the other person signs.

choices.label: Keep trading on your own account

outcome.text: You decline the partnership and preserve your independent standing. {{other}} is left with the entire silence to finance.

title: THE SCALE THAT WEIGHS HONOUR
text: {{other}} challenges your measures by putting an empty purse on the scales and declaring your honesty too light.

choices.label: Invite three ordinary customers to test the measure

outcome.text: You demonstrate the measure and gain guild standing. {{other}} discovers that an audience can have a use besides laughing.

choices.label: Answer the insult with a better one

outcome.text: You win attention and gain a workplace rival. Your performance slips while you keep supplying new material.

title: THE WOOL WHICH MOVES BY ITSELF
text: {{other}} offers a cheap consignment of wool. A sleeve emerges from the sack before its owner, and several moths emerge before either.

outcome.text: {{other}} says you are missing an opportunity. A moth leaves the sample at that moment, having taken its share already.

choices.label: Buy a small lot for honest salvage (5g)

outcome.text: You buy the usable remnants and sort the damage honestly. {{other}} objects to your description chiefly because it explains the price.

choices.label: Sell it on without disclosing the damage

outcome.text: You earn nine gold and gain a fraud complaint. The moths prove more candid witnesses than your description.

title: THE EEL IN THE RENT ROLL
text: {{other}} reads a customary rent that includes one eel per strip. The stream has been dry for two summers. Tradition, the explanation goes, is not responsible for water.

choices.label: Petition for a money equivalent based on actual prices

outcome.text: The neighbours sign your petition. {{other}} is asked to explain which part of the impossible eel can be accepted in payment.

choices.label: Pay five gold to settle this year’s demand

outcome.text: You settle the demand in coin. {{other}} accepts a form of eel that is much easier to keep in a purse.

title: THE PLOUGH’S DAY OF REST
text: {{other}} insists that a damaged plough must rest on a saint’s day. The plough has been resting all week; the field is less devout.

choices.label: Repair the plough before the next working day

outcome.text: You repair the plough during the rest day. {{other}} praises the work after confirming that admiration does not count as joining it.

choices.label: Observe the day and accept the lost work

outcome.text: The field waits and you keep the observance. {{other}} approves a sacrifice for which the accounts can supply an exact measure.

choices.label: Borrow sound equipment on a clear promise

outcome.text: You complete the work and gain a real six-gold obligation. The borrowed blade is sharper than the distinction between favour and debt.

title: THE HAYSTACK’S OWNER
text: {{other}} claims a haystack by counting how many people watched it being built. You counted the days you worked on it.

choices.label: Bring a clear account of the labour

outcome.text: You defend your work and gain public standing. {{other}} dislikes an account that cannot be enlarged by inviting friends.

choices.label: Accept a smaller share to avoid losing the whole season

outcome.text: You concede some household food and improve your working relationship. It is a peace with a visible price.

title: THE PRICE OF A MISSING NOT
text: {{other}} asks you to copy an agreement whose most expensive word is “not.” The draft fee increases if you happen to omit it.

outcome.text: You restore “not”. {{other}} discovers that the smallest word on the page has become the largest difficulty in the case.

choices.label: Take the dishonest fee and omit it

outcome.text: Twelve gold buys one absent word. The clerk makes room for it again beneath the heading for forgery.

choices.label: Require both parties to approve the new wording

outcome.text: You force the proposed change into the open. Your reputation and experience rise; the secret fee disappears.

title: THE TWO ORIGINAL COPIES
text: {{other}} brings two “original” deeds that disagree about a field. Both carry the same date, ink and confident assertion of uniqueness.

outcome.text: You compare the hands, dates and seals. {{other}} has to wait for an answer capable of surviving a second copy.

choices.label: Endorse the more profitable copy without inquiry

outcome.text: You create a fraud charge and lose guild standing. The other original remains inconveniently original.

title: THE CERTIFICATE OF EXCELLENT HEALTH
text: {{other}} wants a certificate saying you found no illness. The requested wording includes a date on which you never examined anyone.

choices.label: Offer a real examination and an accurate report

outcome.text: You insist on examining a person rather than a date. {{other}} looks offended until asked which one they would prefer treated.
You receive seventeen gold and a fraud charge. Your employment is lost when the false certificate is challenged.
The convenient certificate remains unsigned. {{other}} must find a physician whose memory can be hired separately from their eyes.

title: THE CONSULTATION JAR
text: {{other}} brings a sealed jar for diagnosis and admits, after some questioning, that three households contributed to it to save the consultation fee.

choices.label: Explain why the samples must be separate

outcome.text: You label the jar and separate it from the diagnosis. {{other}} admits the patient may require more attention than the container.

choices.label: Give one confident diagnosis for everyone

outcome.text: Your performance and professional standing fall. The certainty is remembered; a genuine cure has not taken place.

title: THE PATRON’S IMPROVED LAST VERSE
text: {{other}} wants your performance to end with a direct accusation of treason against a powerful household. The patron describes the risk as literary.

choices.label: Refuse to turn a rhyme into testimony

outcome.text: The patron takes back the underlined verse. For once your safest line is the one nobody will hear you recite.

choices.label: Perform the accusation (risk prison and dismissal)

success.text: The hall treats the verse as satire and you earn nineteen gold. {{other}} applauds the boldness from a comfortable distance.

failure.text: The accusation is treated as a deliberate falsehood. You lose your employment and are imprisoned for the performance.

choices.label: Offer a verse about the patron’s own courage

outcome.text: You turn the proposed risk back toward its owner. Your reputation rises; {{other}} declines the opportunity to become the subject.

title: THE SONG PAID FOR BY THE PAUSE
text: {{other}} offers to pay you to stop between verses so a rival performer can be heard from the next yard. It is the first time your silence has received a proper offer.

outcome.text: You make room for the second performance and gain a cooperative reputation. {{other}} appreciates having arranged something without a feud.

choices.label: Sing straight through the rival’s turn

outcome.text: You win attention and damage your professional standing. {{other}} now knows which agreements require a louder bell.

title: THE LETTER IN THE SAND BOX
text: {{other}} wants you to dry a confidential letter over sand that will preserve an impression of its contents. Curiosity has supplied its own copying method.

choices.label: Use fresh sand and destroy the impression

outcome.text: You protect the confidence and improve your performance. {{other}} dislikes the tidy disposal of an opportunity.

choices.label: Keep the impression for future leverage

outcome.text: You create a concealed record and a secret about your conduct. Your work gains experience in a direction a good patron would not recommend.

choices.label: Tell the sender what was proposed

outcome.text: You expose the trick, gain standing and acquire a workplace rival. {{other}} has learned something about the speed of letters.

title: THE BOOTS FOR THE LEFT FOOT
text: {{other}} brings a company supply order for boots. Every pair contains two left feet, which the contractor describes as excellent uniformity.

choices.label: Reject the issue before the company marches

outcome.text: The company inspects the boots and starts laughing with both feet. {{other}} seeks a buyer less committed to having a left and a right.

choices.label: Rework the issue with the company cobbler

outcome.text: You work through the repair with sore hands. The men can march; praise is confined to the admirable discovery of two directions.

choices.label: Certify the issue and take the dishonest fee

outcome.text: You earn thirteen gold and create a supply-fraud charge. The evidence walks badly but reaches the clerk.

title: THE BAND’S HONEST ACCOUNTANT
text: {{other}} has drawn up an impeccably fair division of loot. Unfortunately the calculation includes goods nobody has stolen yet.

choices.label: Divide only what is actually available

outcome.text: You remove the goods nobody has stolen yet. {{other}} concedes that an honest account is a useful precaution in a dishonest profession.

choices.label: Promise your share of the imagined haul

outcome.text: The band approves the advance. Fourteen gold is entered as your obligation, the first entirely genuine item on the page.

choices.label: Take a larger share through a false count

outcome.text: You take ten gold. {{other}} corrects the account without a clerk, beginning with a very clear description of you.

familyFeud.reason: A false division of the band’s proceeds

title: THE ROYAL FEAST OF DISASTER
text: A visiting envoy’s falcon has been served at supper. {{other}} recognises its silver ring and offers to say it was a diplomatic gift if you will support the story. The cook offers the remaining wing.

choices.label: Admit the disaster and fund compensation (16g)

outcome.text: The compensation is paid. {{other}} accepts an honest account of the bird’s final journey, while the cook quietly removes the remaining wing.
You accuse {{other}} and damage that relationship into a rivalry. Your own family gains an enemy household; the falcon gains no useful explanation.

familyFeud.reason: A false accusation over the envoy’s falcon

choices.label: Insist on an accurate account without promising funds

outcome.text: You insist on an accurate account. {{other}} signs it with the expression of someone being asked to recognise dinner as a diplomatic document.

title: THE PORTRAIT THAT EXPECTS A BOW
text: {{other}} wants visitors to bow to a newly painted likeness before seeing its owner. The portrait has the more forgiving expression.

choices.label: Bow to the painted rank and save your quarrel

outcome.text: {{other}} is delighted by your salute. The portrait accepts it with rather less need for encouragement.

choices.label: Address only the person who can answer

outcome.text: {{other}} becomes your rival. The portrait has acquired a considerably more agreeable social circle than its owner.
The compliment reaches {{other}} a moment late. You gain charm and lose a little trust in the room.

title: THE CELLAR BELOW THE PRECEDENT
text: {{other}} claims your household must keep storing grain in a cellar that floods. The right to use it is ancient; the water is fresh.

choices.label: Pay to drain and repair the store (22g)

outcome.text: The stores are raised and the water kept out. {{other}} accepts a change in custom once custom has stopped smelling of wet grain.

choices.label: Insist that inherited rights need no repair

outcome.text: You keep the money. The household keeps its ancient right to a cellar now occupied chiefly by water.

choices.label: Move the argument into a public petition

outcome.text: The neighbours support the complaint. {{other}} asks whether the accumulated rights can also be expected to carry the buckets.

title: THE ANCESTOR WHO CHANGED SIDES
text: {{other}} offers to improve your pedigree by inserting a famous commander. Unfortunately the commander fought against the Crown your family currently serves.

outcome.text: You retain an honest family account and improve Crown standing. {{other}} must sell the commander to a household with different loyalties.
Your family enjoys a brief rise in standing and gains a concealed false lineage. The document can now be challenged as a forgery.

title: THE COUNCIL CHAIR AT AUCTION
text: {{other}} is selling the right to sit in a chair outside the council room. The wording is careful about which side of the door it is on.

choices.label: Read the grant aloud before the bidding

outcome.text: You expose the limited claim and gain Crown standing. {{other}} loses trust in your appreciation of furniture.

choices.label: Buy the public appearance of access (10g)

outcome.text: You pay ten gold for a conspicuous seat, not an office. Your family’s reputation rises slightly; the council seals stay with their holders.

choices.label: Remain standing and keep the money

outcome.text: You decline the chair. {{other}} cannot decide whether you are poor or unusually well informed.

title: THE AMBASSADOR’S BLANK PAGE
text: {{other}} asks you to witness a document before its terms are filled in. The argument for speed is that peace is too important to wait for words.

outcome.text: You gain standing for refusing a blank commitment. {{other}} must interrupt the urgency long enough to say what it is for.

choices.label: Witness the blank and hope for favourable terms

outcome.text: You become party to a fraudulent instrument and acquire a legal charge. Peace has been given an alarmingly broad margin.

charge.offence: Witnessing a knowingly blank diplomatic instrument

choices.label: Offer to copy complete terms under witnesses

outcome.text: You improve Crown standing and professional judgement without promising a treaty no one has written.

title: THE HUNT THAT STOPPED AT AN ALTAR
text: {{other}}’s hunting party has cornered a deer beside a wayside altar. Several people are arguing about sanctuary; the deer appears strongly in favour.

choices.label: Ask the party to leave the animal alone

outcome.text: You gain Church standing and lose hunting favour with {{other}}. The altar keeps the quieter congregation.

choices.label: Fund a meal instead of the disputed hunt (8g)

outcome.text: You pay for supper and lower local religious tension. {{other}} accepts a peace that comes with a table.

title: THE PRICE OF THE THIRD WHISPER
text: {{other}} offers you a secret whose first two buyers are standing across the hall. Both look disappointed to find the information still available.

choices.label: Refuse to become the third exclusive owner

outcome.text: You ask to meet the other exclusive owners. {{other}} withdraws the offer before exclusivity can become a public meeting.

choices.label: Pay for the rumour, knowing it may be worthless (5g)

outcome.text: You pay five gold for an unverified rumour. No actual secret is revealed merely because someone priced it as one.

choices.label: Tell the buyers they have been sold exclusivity together

outcome.text: You expose the sales trick and gain a named rival. {{other}} is forced to offer a less crowded form of discretion.

title: THE ARMOUR FOR A SMALLER ANCESTOR
text: {{other}} offers you ancestral armour for a ceremonial ride. The breastplate remembers a slimmer family.

choices.label: Pay to fit the armour safely (11g)

outcome.text: You pay for alteration rather than for endurance. {{other}} admires the result without admitting it needed work.

choices.label: Ride in the tight armour (risk a crushed fall)

success.text: You survive the ride and acquire a modest reputation for composure. Nobody sees how slowly you take your next breath.

failure.text: You fall badly when the armour prevents a safe dismount. A broken bone makes the family resemblance newly painful.

choices.label: Ride in your own ordinary clothes

outcome.text: You avoid the injury and lose some of {{other}}’s ceremonial favour. Your ancestors will have to be recognised by your face.

title: THE CHILD’S LARGE SIGNATURE
text: {{other}} asks you to endorse an order attributed to the young ruler. The handwriting is a fine adult hand, except where someone has added an ornamental blot.

outcome.text: You improve Crown standing by asking for lawful confirmation. {{other}} dislikes the number of adults now reading the order.
You create a forgery charge and gain favour with {{other}}. The blot has not made the document any younger.

title: THE GUEST WHO COMES WITH A RANSOM
text: {{other}} wants you to keep a “guest” until a disputed ransom is paid. The guest has asked why hospitality requires a barred door.

choices.label: Refuse to make your household a private prison

outcome.text: You gain public standing and lose favour with {{other}}. Your doors remain useful for entering as well as leaving.
You acquire a charge for aiding unlawful detention. {{other}} calls you a dependable host. The description is entered among the evidence.
You pay to convene a negotiation and gain Crown standing. No ransom is declared settled until the parties actually agree.

title: THE MAP WITH AN OBEDIENT RIVER
text: {{other}} presents a map on which a boundary river bends conveniently around a disputed estate. The actual river has not been consulted.

choices.label: Insist on a new survey rather than a better drawing

outcome.text: You gain standing and anger {{other}} by distinguishing a claim from geography.
You create a boundary-fraud charge. {{other}} gains confidence in you while the evidence acquires a riverbank.

charge.offence: Attesting a knowingly false boundary map

title: THE COLOURS OF YOUR ENEMY
text: {{other}} has ordered banners using your family’s colours in the order worn by a rival household. The herald says the difference is obvious once someone starts fighting.

choices.label: Pay to correct them before the procession (7g)

outcome.text: You pay for the correction and improve your household’s public standing. {{other}} thanks you for solving the argument before it needed a wound.

choices.label: Carry plain banners and explain the mistake

outcome.text: You avoid a false claim at a small cost to public dignity. The family’s reputation for honesty improves.

choices.label: Use the confusion to provoke the other household

outcome.text: You damage public order and create a lasting family feud with {{other}} over the deliberate provocation.

title: THE MUSTER OF THE ABSENT MEN
text: {{other}} submits a list of fighting men that includes a grandfather, a departed groom and one name written twice with different hats.

outcome.text: You improve Crown standing and offend {{other}}. The force becomes smaller on paper and no smaller in the field.

choices.label: Certify the full list for a fee

outcome.text: You earn fifteen gold and acquire a military fraud charge. No extra soldiers emerge from the new ink.
You spend twelve gold and slightly reduce war threat. {{other}} approves of a remedy paid for in someone else’s coin.

title: THE TOAST TO YOUR GOOD FORTUNE
text: {{other}} drinks to your future success while quietly suggesting it would be kinder if you found it elsewhere.

choices.label: Ask openly what your rival wants

outcome.text: You turn the insinuation into a clear disagreement. Public reputation improves while {{other}}’s affection falls.

choices.label: Offer a limited truce without a new alliance

outcome.text: You improve trust with {{other}}. The households do not acquire an alliance merely because the drinking is less hostile.

choices.label: Reply with a toast they cannot mistake

outcome.text: You gain a little charm and deepen the rivalry. {{other}} now has a sentence worth repeating accurately.

title: THE CHAPEL WITH YOUR NAME ON IT
text: {{other}} proposes a lavish family memorial while your household’s roof needs repair. The plan gives your name excellent shelter and your family rather less.

outcome.text: The living household receives a better roof. {{other}} keeps the memorial drawing dry beneath it and finds the arrangement artistically disappointing.
The dedication is paid for. A mason spells your name correctly while rain continues to have difficulty recognising it at home.
{{other}} leaves with both estimates. The rain submits its own argument without waiting for your patronage.

title: THE TASTER’S FINAL OBJECTION
text: Your taster refuses a cup offered by {{other}}. The objection is unusually specific: the same mixture killed the rats behind the kitchen.

choices.label: Have the cup removed and preserve it as evidence

outcome.text: You avoid the danger and make {{other}} a rival. No conviction follows merely from your suspicion.

success.text: The drink is merely foul. Your confidence impresses the room and injures your health, which has not been asked for an opinion.

failure.text: The taster was right about the mixture. Royal confidence cannot persuade your body to survive it.

effects.death: Died after drinking a cup explicitly suspected of poison.

choices.label: Pay for an independent inquiry (15 treasury)

outcome.text: You fund an inquiry and improve public order. {{other}} resents a suspicion that now has a budget.

title: THE AUCTION OF YOUR SUCCESSION
text: {{other}} asks what it would cost to become your heir. The offer is accompanied by a list of improvements to your eventual funeral.

choices.label: Reject the purchase and publish the approach

outcome.text: You publish the offer and return the funeral improvements. {{other}} discovers how awkward it is to accuse a ruler of refusing a bribe.

choices.label: Take a personal payment without changing the succession

outcome.text: You pocket thirty gold and leave the succession untouched. {{other}} keeps quiet for now; the payment is recorded as a bribe, not a claim.

charge.offence: Taking a bribe over a promised succession

choices.label: Abdicate to the documented eligible successor

outcome.text: You surrender the crown through the recorded succession. {{other}} receives no special appointment for having brought a price list.

title: THE LIGHTER ROYAL FACE
text: {{other}} proposes lightening the coin while leaving your portrait large enough to inspire confidence. The proposed saving is almost entirely silver.

choices.label: Keep the standard and publish the accounts

outcome.text: The standard remains. {{other}} withdraws the suggestion that your face could be made to circulate in place of silver.
The royal treasury gains forty gold while public order and family standing fall. The accusation of fraud bears your seal as clearly as the coins bear your face.

charge.offence: Ordering a dishonest issue of coin

outcome.text: Twenty treasury gold buys relief. {{other}} watches the money leave without finding any opportunity to make it lighter.

title: THE VERDICT DELIVERED BEFORE THE WITNESSES
text: {{other}} asks you to approve a private condemnation before hearing evidence. It would save the council a morning. The saving is offered as a reason to take a life.

choices.label: Require evidence and leave the person alive

outcome.text: The petition must wait for evidence. {{other}} is distressed to discover that the witnesses have been invited to contribute something.

choices.label: Condemn the named petitioner instead (death and a family feud)

outcome.text: You order {{other}}’s death. The person dies, public order falls and the household feud outlives the audience.

familyFeud.reason: A summary royal execution without evidence

choices.label: Dismiss the petition without deciding the case

outcome.text: You leave the accusation unproved and gain a little public standing. {{other}} has saved neither a morning nor an enemy.

title: THE SAINT’S SMALLER SKULL
text: {{other}} displays a saint’s skull beside a smaller skull said to belong to the saint as a child. The keeper has anticipated the obvious objection and looks tired of it.

choices.label: Ask for the history of both objects

outcome.text: You expose the weak account without inventing a miracle. Your reputation improves and {{other}} becomes less welcoming to questions.

choices.label: Leave the objects and give alms instead (4g)

outcome.text: You give four gold toward relief rather than the display. Your faith and family standing improve without acquiring an extra saint.

choices.label: Write an endorsement you know is false

outcome.text: You lend your name to the false display and create a fraud charge. The smaller skull has acquired an adult witness.

title: THE ANIMAL DECLARED A FISH
text: {{other}} supports declaring a barnyard animal a fish so it may be eaten on fast days. The proposed proof is that it has once stood in a puddle.

choices.label: Ask why the puddle did not convert its owner

outcome.text: {{other}} is asked whether the animal must swim before the classification takes effect. The argument becomes much less comfortable near the trough.

choices.label: Keep the fast without policing everyone’s supper

outcome.text: You keep your own observance and let the meal remain a meal. {{other}} puts away a defence longer than the animal’s pedigree.

title: THE OVEN OF INNOCENCE
text: {{other}} wants to settle an accusation by having you touch a heated oven door. The oven is said to know the truth. Nobody has explained how it will communicate it.

choices.label: Demand witnesses rather than an injury

outcome.text: You ask which part of the oven can identify a liar. {{other}} objects to your tone; the baker would like the bread space back.

choices.label: Submit to the burning ordeal (lasting pain)

outcome.text: You burn your hand and develop chronic pain. {{other}} admires your endurance. The admiration does nothing for the hand.

choices.label: Pay for a formal petition instead (11g)

outcome.text: Your petition asks for ordinary testimony. {{other}} dislikes an objection that can be examined without warming the room.

title: THE PILGRIMAGE MEASURED IN RENT
text: {{other}} offers to make a pilgrimage on your behalf for a fee determined by how sinful you look. The route gets longer as you explain your finances.

choices.label: Make a modest local pilgrimage yourself

outcome.text: You take the modest road yourself. {{other}} loses a customer and the power to add another mile whenever your purse is mentioned.

choices.label: Contribute to a genuine traveller’s expenses (7g)

outcome.text: You give seven gold without claiming that another person’s miles cancel your conduct. {{other}} appreciates an honest purpose for the journey.
You ask whether the return journey also reduces your sins. {{other}} decides that your soul requires a different sort of customer.

title: THE FUNERAL’S PRICE OF SILENCE
text: {{other}} is collecting for a neighbour’s burial. The fee for leaving out an embarrassing story is higher than the fee for telling any number of flattering ones.

choices.label: Pay toward a plain, respectful burial (5g)

outcome.text: You give five gold toward the burial and improve family standing. The dead are not made more virtuous by being more expensive.

choices.label: Refuse to pay for withholding gossip

outcome.text: You challenge the charge and lose {{other}}’s affection. Your own reputation improves for making the objection before anyone starts the story.

choices.label: Supply a better story to lower your share

outcome.text: You spread private gossip and gain a rival in {{other}}, who no longer trusts you with an account that might reach the next funeral.

title: THE KEY TO CHARITY
text: {{other}} holds the key to a food chest and insists it cannot be opened until the donors’ names are read. Hungry people are waiting through an exceptionally generous list.

choices.label: Offer to read the names while food is served

outcome.text: You help the distribution without emptying your own household stores. Church standing and {{other}}’s trust improve.

choices.label: Supply food from your own household reserve

outcome.text: Your household gives up food and gains reputation. {{other}} sees a donation delivered without first hearing its name.

choices.label: Make a public account of the delay

outcome.text: You record the hungry households waiting outside. {{other}} discovers that a key can keep a door shut without keeping an account private.

title: THE MIRACLE OF THE DRY PARCHMENT
text: Rain avoids the shrine’s best account book because {{other}} keeps it under the only sound section of roof. The rest of the room is being called a test of faith.

choices.label: Fund repairs instead of another miracle plaque (10g)

outcome.text: Your contribution pays for the work. {{other}} records the coin, which has achieved rather more than the dry parchment did.

choices.label: Point out the useful location of the ledger

outcome.text: You inspect the wonderfully dry record while the roof drips nearby. {{other}} finds your choice of comparison unhelpful.

title: THE BRIDGE THAT REQUIRES FAITH
