text: The muster clerk looks at your destrier, then at his roll, and informs you that a man with a warhorse serves mounted, at his own cost, for twice the term.

choices.label: Serve mounted and be seen doing it

outcome.text: You ride out at the head of the Swineford contingent, which is four men and a cart. It is absurd and it is remembered.
You keep the horse and the clerk keeps a note. Both of you know the horse is sound and neither of you says so.

title: THEY HAVE HEARD ABOUT THE RELIC
text: Three pilgrims are at your gate before Prime, having walked from Ely on the strength of a rumour about what you keep in your house.

choices.label: Let them see it, and take nothing

outcome.text: They stay an hour and leave weeping. By Lammas there are thirty of them, and by Michaelmas the road past your door is a road.
They pay it. Word of the penny travels exactly as fast as word of the relic, and arrives in the same conversation.

choices.label: Send them on to the abbey

outcome.text: You point them up the road and shut the gate. They go, and they tell the abbey where they were sent from.

title: A MAN WHO KEEPS A LEDGER
text: Word has got round that you keep written accounts. The reeve arrives with a box of tallies, an apologetic expression, and no intention of leaving with the box.

outcome.text: Nine evenings of somebody else’s arithmetic. You find two errors in the parish’s favour and one very much not, and you report both.
Four shillings and the work is done properly. The reeve pays and thereafter treats you as a tradesman rather than a neighbour.
The accounts balance beautifully and two of the entries are yours. It will hold until somebody else learns to read a tally.

title: A STONE OF THINE OWN
text: Your own millstone means your own flour, and half the lane has worked that out. They arrive with sacks and a hopeful manner.

choices.label: Grind for them, and take no toll

outcome.text: You grind for nine households and take nothing. The miller hears about it within the day and is not amused.
A twentieth, measured in front of them. The mill takes a tenth and everybody knows it, so you are paid and nobody feels robbed.
You shut the door on them. It is entirely your stone and they go back to the mill, past your house, every week, for years.

title: THE ONE WITH THE MASK
text: Sickness is in the row by the ford and you own the only beaked mask in the parish, which in everyone else’s eyes makes you the nearest thing Swineford has to a physician.

choices.label: Put it on and go in

outcome.text: The mask does nothing at all and the vinegar-soaked rag inside it may do a little. You bring four people through and take a cough that lasts till spring.
She takes it without comment and uses it for nine years. You never get it back and never ask.
You are well all season. The lane knows exactly what is hanging on your door and exactly who did not come.

title: A MAN WITH A SWORD IS ASKED
text: A carter is being beaten in the market by two men over a debt. You are wearing a sword, which the whole market has noticed, and which changes what standing still means.

outcome.text: They go. Nobody is cut and everybody saw the steel come out, and you will be answering for that at the tourn.

choices.label: Put a hand on the hilt and say nothing

outcome.text: They look at the hand, then at your face, and decide the debt can wait. Not one word is spoken and it works completely.
You walk on wearing a sword past a man being beaten. The market watches you do it and draws the obvious conclusion.

title: THE FORESTER LOOKS AT THY HOUND
text: The forester stops you on the coppice road and looks a long time at your hunting hound. Under forest law a dog that can run down a deer must be lawed: three claws off the forefoot.

outcome.text: It is done at the next swanimote with a mallet and a chisel. The dog lives, limps, and never runs anything down again.
Twelve shillings buys the dog its claws and buys the forester a new opinion of your purse. He will be back.

choices.label: Keep the dog out of the wood

outcome.text: The hound never goes near the coppice again and neither do you. It is a small life for a good dog and it keeps all four feet.

title: THE COUNCILLOR’S CREATIVE ACCOUNTS
text: s=>{const scandal=s.world.court?.scandals.find(c=>!c.resolved);const person=s.world.characters[scandal?.actorId??""];return`${person?.name??"Your councillor"}, your ${scandal?.office.replaceAll("_"," ")??"official"}, has diverted ${scandal?.amount??0} treasury gold. The account describes national security. The receipt describes decorative horses. A family ally asks whether the horses could be classified as cavalry.`}

outcome.text: The inquiry removes the responsible official and recovers half the missing funds. The household’s supporters take the dismissal personally.
The official keeps the seal and owes you a favour. The original receipts remain in someone else’s hands.
The treasurer loses the seal. The guilds recognise an injustice considerably faster than the council recognises a sum.
The seal returns to your keeping. The missing gold does not. The dismissed official takes the grievance home.

title: THE CONTESTED SEAL
text: s=>{const q=s.world.court?.petition;return q&&!q.resolved?`Your request for the ${q.office.replaceAll("_"," ")}\u2019s seal is before the ruler. ${(0,import_courtPolitics.petitionProspects)(s,"merit").detail} Appointment depends on the council\u2019s decision.`:"The court has already recorded this petition."}

outcome.text: The ruler considers your service against the vacancy, incumbent and rival candidates. The court record gives the decision.

choices.label: Ask your patron to speak for you

outcome.text: Your patron addresses the council. Their support helps; the incumbent still has a case to answer.

choices.label: Offer further service before a new petition

outcome.text: The ruler records a condition of further professional service. You receive a target rather than a seal.
The request is withdrawn. The existing officeholder remains responsible.

title: THE OPPOSING HOUSEHOLDS
text: s=>{const q=(0,import_courtPolitics.oppositionAudienceCoalition)(s);return`${s.world.characters[q?.leaderId??""]?.name??"An opposing household"} brings a coalition before the council${q?.claimantId?` backing ${s.world.characters[q.claimantId]?.name}'s claim`:""}. Their strength is ${q?.strength??0}. They have withheld cooperation and demand an answer.${s.world.court?.crisis&&s.world.court.crisis.responseYear===void 0&&s.world.court?.crisis?.leaderId===q?.leaderId?" Your reign is in crisis. After your response, you may lose the crown next year if legitimacy stays below 15, public order below 25 and coalition strength at least 40. A settlement reduces strength by 20; a hearing by 8; dismissal adds 12.":""}`}

outcome.text: A recorded settlement reduces the coalition’s strength. Rival claims remain in the family record.
The hearing earns some respect and eases opposition while leaving the dispute open.

choices.label: Assert royal authority and dismiss them

outcome.text: The rejected petition becomes a rallying point. The coalition gains strength and public order falls.

title: THE DYER’S BLUE DEBT
text: {{client}} offers a winter’s cloth on credit. The blue dye washes out in rain. {{rival}} has already promised to sell it as royal indigo.

outcome.text: You test and mark the cloth honestly. The blue remains in the water rather than the warranty; the buyers pay for what you can defend.

choices.label: Sell it before the weather turns

outcome.text: You collect the fees and make a powerful enemy of the first damp customer. The retained sample is a very portable accusation.

choices.label: Pay a dyer to fix the cloth

outcome.text: Your hired dyer corrects the cloth before delivery. The colour stays where it belongs, which is a novel basis for a trading concern.

title: THE RIVAL’S LAST BALE
text: {{rival}} claims that {{client}}’s wool bears a stolen mark. The guild may seize the entire consignment, including your stake.

outcome.text: The shepherd identifies the flock and the mark. The rival’s claim collapses under the testimony of a man less impressively dressed.
You buy silence and keep the stock. Your rival keeps enough evidence to make the silence expensive to maintain.

choices.label: Hire a clerk to trace the sales

outcome.text: Your clerk traces the bales through every sale. The title is recorded before anyone can add another ingenious owner.

title: THE FUNERAL BELL WARRANTY
text: {{client}} orders a bell guaranteed to outlive the abbot. The mould is cracked. {{rival}} offers a coat of paint and a quiet blessing.

outcome.text: The recast bell rings soundly. The abbot asks about the warranty; you point out that the bell has already survived his longest speech.

choices.label: Conceal the crack beneath the inscription

outcome.text: The bell rings badly beneath its handsome inscription. You keep the fee and acquire a customer who can demonstrate the defect to the whole parish.

choices.label: Hire an apprentice for a second casting

outcome.text: The apprentice helps cast a sound bell and stays in your service. The wardens grudgingly approve work whose second pair of hands has been paid.

title: THE WIDOW’S WORKSHOP
text: {{client}} keeps a workshop after the master’s burial. {{rival}} petitions the guild to confiscate the tools before the candles burn down.

outcome.text: The charter protects the workshop. The rival has to find a living master to rob of commissions, an irritating restriction on enterprise.
You take the contracts. The widow keeps the charter and an exact account of the kindness your competitors can expect.

choices.label: Pay a clerk to establish the succession

outcome.text: Your clerk records the succession and takes paid work with you. The tools stay where their owner can use them.

title: THE PHYSICIAN’S GREAT SUCCESS
text: {{client}} asks you to organise care for a household. {{rival}} advertises expensive bloodletting without first asking who is ill. Your own record must distinguish actual symptoms from preventive advice.

outcome.text: You record the actual needs and arrange care. Your practice earns confidence without having to declare healthy people dramatically cured.

choices.label: Accept every patient and every fee

outcome.text: You take too many fees and spread your care too thinly. A complaint arrives with a much more reliable record of your promises.
Your paid assistant takes routine work under supervision. Care is recorded for review; nobody is promised a recovery merely because help has arrived.

title: THE WELL OF SAINT ITCH
text: Fever follows the water sold by {{client}} as a saint’s blessing. {{rival}} proposes charging double for blessed leeches.

choices.label: Inspect the well and separate the sick

outcome.text: You document the water risk and arrange safer care. The well keeper is asked to explain why a blessing needs to stand downhill from a privy.
You collect the fees. Harmful treatment leaves an actual complaint wherever illness made the treatment more than an expensive performance.

choices.label: Pay an assistant to boil cloth and water

outcome.text: Your paid assistant supplies clean cloth and safer water. Fever pressure falls; ongoing patients remain under care rather than being cured by the account.

title: THE TITHE OF THE DEAD
text: {{client}} discovers that the abbey charges burial tithe on bones washed out of last year’s graves. {{rival}} calls this recurring revenue.

outcome.text: The burial roll is corrected. One tanner ceases to be the abbey’s most reliable repeat customer.
The collectors keep their silver and the households keep their anger. Your improved connection with the former is noted carefully by the latter.

choices.label: Pay a clerk to reconcile the burial roll

outcome.text: Your clerk reconciles the burial entries and stays in paid service. The dead are allowed to stop financing their own paperwork.

title: THE SAINT’S HORSE TOOTH
text: {{client}} seeks a ruling on the priory’s newest relic. {{rival}} has already sold indulgences for venerating what looks remarkably like a horse’s tooth.

choices.label: Submit the relic to an honest inquiry

outcome.text: The inquiry rejects the horse tooth’s saintly pedigree. The stable boy supplies the most useful evidence without once consulting Latin.
The display remains profitable. The stable boy recognises the tooth, and your rival recognises what that knowledge is worth.

choices.label: Hire a scholar to examine its provenance

outcome.text: The hired scholar establishes the tooth’s provenance and joins your service. The horse loses a canonisation; the record gains a species.

title: THE COMPANY AT THE BROKEN BRIDGE
text: {{client}} brings orders to cross a broken bridge before dawn. {{rival}} proposes sending the levy first to test its strength.

choices.label: Find a ford and protect the levy

outcome.text: The company uses the ford and avoids the broken bridge. You earn command credit for a route with fewer opportunities to become a memorial.

choices.label: Force the crossing before the enemy arrives

outcome.text: The crossing is forced and the operation harms the client entrusted to your command. You collect the fee; your surviving witnesses keep their account.

choices.label: Pay engineers to shore the bridge

outcome.text: Your paid engineer shores the bridge and remains with the company. The convoy crosses something more substantial than confidence.

title: THE CAPTIVES’ EMPTY PURSES
text: {{client}} brings three captured scouts. {{rival}} insists they are noblemen in unusually convincing poverty.

choices.label: Exchange them for your missing soldiers

outcome.text: The exchange is recorded and your service recognised. The clerk is asked to count returned people rather than the social importance of their boots.

choices.label: Extort a ransom from their families

outcome.text: The ransom brings profit and a feud between the households concerned. Your rival keeps the demand, complete with your excellent signature.

choices.label: Hire a clerk to verify their names

outcome.text: Your hired clerk verifies the names and records the exchange. The captives lose their imaginary nobility before it can be priced.

title: THE CHANCELLOR’S SALTED CAMEL
text: {{client}} sends a draft levy taxing every salt camel. The realm has no camels. {{rival}} recommends retaining the revenue estimate.

choices.label: Rewrite the levy around actual trade

outcome.text: The levy is corrected around real trade. The treasury benefits and the council reluctantly admits that a camel is a poor source of local revenue.
You take exemption fees and leave an account your rival can read. The treasury has less silver and an exceptionally well-documented camel.

choices.label: Hire a clerk to survey the ports

outcome.text: Your hired clerk surveys the ports and stays in service. The decree acquires actual cargoes, which are less picturesque and considerably more taxable.

title: THE DEAD FALCONER’S WAGES
text: {{client}} pays a falconer dead these nine years. {{rival}} claims the hawks remain loyal enough to justify his wages.

choices.label: Expose the accounts to the council

outcome.text: The false wages are recovered into the treasury. The hawks decline to testify about the last nine years of their employer’s work.

choices.label: Sell your silence to the beneficiary

outcome.text: You take hush money. Your rival keeps the burial entry beside the wage account, two documents that have finally found someone alive to blame.

choices.label: Hire an auditor to follow the payments

outcome.text: The paid auditor follows the payments and joins your service. The treasury recovers funds; the glove on its cushion is excused further duty.

title: ROTATE THE STRIPS
text: {{client}} brings a thin harvest from exhausted strips. {{rival}} has offered a new rotation without testing the soil.

outcome.text: You mark a trial strip and record the soil before committing seed.
The whole strip is planted under your new plan; the harvest will test its ambition.
The tenants compare their observations with yours before the rotation is agreed.

title: NEGOTIATE A TENANCY
text: {{client}} needs a rent agreement that survives a poor harvest. The landlord wants a fixed payment even if the seed fails.

outcome.text: The harvest tally becomes the basis of your proposed rent.
Your demand for a lower rent puts the landlord’s agent on the defensive.
The neighbour brings both parties’ accounts to the negotiation.

title: INSPECT THE LIVESTOCK
text: {{client}} brings news of coughing livestock. No one has yet established whether the illness has spread beyond one stall.

choices.label: Inspect and isolate the sick animals

outcome.text: You examine the coughing animals separately and record what you find.

choices.label: Return the herd to work quickly

outcome.text: The owner is asked to return the herd to work before every uncertainty is settled.

choices.label: Ask a herder to review the symptoms

outcome.text: A second herder compares the animals’ signs with your notes.

title: ACCEPT A COMMISSION
text: {{client}} orders hinges before a funeral date has been agreed. The metal, dimensions and delivery promise are yours to settle.

outcome.text: The customer receives a delivery plan with measured dimensions and a test piece.
You offer an earlier delivery for a larger fee, accepting a smaller margin for error.

choices.label: Share the work with an apprentice

outcome.text: The apprentice receives a defined part of the commission under your supervision.

title: TEACH AN APPRENTICE
text: {{client}} asks you to train a workshop apprentice. The learner needs supervision, wages and a piece suited to their ability.

outcome.text: The learner starts a trial piece with your hand close enough to stop an error.
You give the learner an independent job that will test their present limits.

choices.label: Pay for a second master’s advice

outcome.text: The second master is paid to inspect the learner’s work alongside yours.

title: CHALLENGE THE GUILD
text: {{client}} disputes a guild assay. {{rival}} wants the hearing held over the inspecting master’s private wine.

outcome.text: A witnessed assay enters the guild record before the hearing.
You challenge the officers in public, making their pride part of the dispute.

choices.label: Seek support from a respected master

outcome.text: A respected master agrees to examine the claim before supporting your petition.

title: NEGOTIATE A GRAIN DEAL
text: {{client}} offers a grain shipment with a disputed measure. Price, quality and the partner’s share must be agreed before loading.

outcome.text: The buyer and seller compare the grain against a witnessed measure.

choices.label: Press for a high margin and rapid shipment

outcome.text: You press for a higher margin and accept the risks of a hurried shipment.

choices.label: Share the shipment with a trading partner

outcome.text: The partner’s cargo and share are written into the shipment agreement.

title: SETTLE THE BRIDGE TOLL
text: {{client}} has a cart held at a bridge charging for six wheels. There are two on the cart, and armed men beside the toll board.

choices.label: Check the toll charter and escort

outcome.text: The keeper receives the toll charter and the convoy’s actual wheel count.

choices.label: Run the disputed crossing at speed

outcome.text: Your cart approaches the crossing quickly enough to limit time for negotiation.
The convoy partners present a joint toll offer with a shared escort.

title: CONTEST A RIVAL’S CLAIM
text: {{rival}} claims the mark on {{client}}’s wool. The shepherd remembers the shearing and expects someone to ask.

choices.label: Present witnesses and the wool marks

outcome.text: The shepherd and wool marks enter the disputed sale’s record.
Your lower offer challenges the rival’s custom as well as their claim.
Both counting houses receive a proposed settlement in writing.

title: DELIVER A SERMON
text: {{client}} asks for a sermon after counterfeit relics divide the parish. Their neighbours disagree about who should be named.

outcome.text: The sermon begins with the parish’s needs and the evidence about the relics.
Your sermon names the suspected offenders before the whole congregation.

choices.label: Ask the parish elder to help reconcile them

outcome.text: The parish elder helps frame a sermon that leaves room for restitution.

title: MEDIATE THE TITHE DISPUTE
text: {{client}} disputes another household’s goose tithe. The old custom is unclear and the archdeacon dislikes an empty purse.

outcome.text: Both households give their account of the goose tithe in the same hearing.
Your support for the stronger household makes their influence part of the settlement.

choices.label: Seek a private settlement with the elder

outcome.text: The elder carries a private proposal between the disputing households.

title: SEEK PARISH RESPONSIBILITY
text: {{client}} can bring your parish work before the archdeacon. {{rival}} has already requested the same responsibility.

outcome.text: The archdeacon receives an account of the parish work you actually completed.
Your patron is asked to press your claim ahead of competing candidates.
You offer to take a supervised parish task before receiving wider responsibility.

title: LEAD A ROAD PATROL
text: {{client}} reports bandits on the road. The reeve’s nephew insists they cannot be there; a familiar tent suggests otherwise.

outcome.text: Scouts return with observations before the patrol takes the road.

negative: Risk of injury to the client

outcome.text: The armed patrol moves directly toward the reported camp.
Local watchmen compare routes and signals with your patrol.

title: ORGANISE THE COMPANY
text: {{client}} brings the company muster. Spears, boots and soldiers appear in three different totals, and the next march is approaching.

outcome.text: The equipment list is checked against the soldiers present at drill.

negative: Risk of injury to the client

outcome.text: The company is ordered into a forced exercise before every shortage is repaired.
Experienced soldiers identify the failures they will have to carry on the march.

title: COMMAND A CONVOY ESCORT
text: {{client}} needs an escort for a supply convoy. A fast route crosses an exposed ford; the longer road needs ration stops.

choices.label: Scout the convoy route and ration stops

outcome.text: The convoy plan names water, cover and ration stops along the scouted road.

choices.label: Race the convoy through the threat

negative: Risk of injury to the client

outcome.text: You accept exposure at the ford in exchange for a faster crossing.
Engineers and soldiers divide the work of protecting the convoy.

title: SEEK A NOBLE PATRON
text: {{client}} will consider patronage if you can offer a useful service. {{rival}} promises access to people neither of you has met.

outcome.text: The proposed service is specific enough for a patron to judge your usefulness.
Your promise of influence reaches beyond your established position.

choices.label: Seek an introduction from a colleague

outcome.text: A colleague carries an introduction and an account of your previous work.

title: ADVISE ON A DECREE
text: {{client}} brings a salt levy that counts the same barrel three times. Changing the draft may offend its author.

choices.label: Compare the decree with actual accounts

outcome.text: The salt draft is compared with the accounts of actual cargoes.

choices.label: Demand the council adopt your draft

outcome.text: You demand the council adopt your correction in front of the original author.
A revised draft circulates privately before the council’s decision.

title: INVESTIGATE COURT ACCOUNTS
text: {{client}} asks you to inspect wages paid to a dead falconer. {{rival}} suggests the hawks remain loyal enough to justify a pension.

outcome.text: The burial entry and wage account are checked before publication.
The beneficiary is confronted before every payment has been traced.

choices.label: Ask another auditor to witness the books

outcome.text: A second auditor signs the checked account beside your name.

title: EXAMINE A PATIENT
text: {{client}} requests an examination. Establish actual symptoms first; a healthy person needs advice rather than an invented disease.

outcome.text: Your examination begins with the person’s own history and observable signs.
You give a rapid opinion and accept responsibility for its certainty.
Another practitioner reviews the observations before an opinion is recorded.

title: TREAT A HOUSEHOLD
text: {{client}} requests care based on the recorded symptoms. Relief depends on the real condition, your preparation and the risks of your method.

outcome.text: Your care follows the actual record and avoids an unnecessary intervention.

negative: Risk of client harm or a professional complaint

outcome.text: You accept the greater risks of a forceful intervention for a hoped-for recovery.
A colleague joins the care plan and agrees a follow-up examination.

title: ORGANISE FEVER RELIEF
text: {{client}} asks you to organise fever relief. The sick households share water, bedding and several contradictory explanations.

choices.label: Trace sick households and clean water

outcome.text: The relief plan traces sick households and the water they share.

choices.label: Order a public purge of suspect goods

outcome.text: A public order calls for suspect goods to be removed before the cause is fully established.
Volunteers arrange beds, clean cloth and separate drinking vessels.

title: PERFORM IN THE HALL
text: {{client}} offers a place in the hall’s programme. The audience likes a fine genealogy and dislikes finding its own scandals in the rhyme.

choices.label: Prepare a piece suited to the audience

outcome.text: You prepare a piece for the audience’s tastes and its known sensitivities.
You improvise before listeners whose generosity is not assured.

choices.label: Share the bill with another performer

outcome.text: The fellow performer receives an agreed place and share of the bill.

title: SEEK A PAYING PATRON
text: {{client}} is considering a place for a performer at their table. Supper, a deposit and the patron’s right to request encores all remain negotiable.

outcome.text: The proposed service is specific enough for a patron to judge your usefulness.
Your promise of influence reaches beyond your established position.

choices.label: Seek an introduction from a colleague

outcome.text: A colleague carries an introduction and an account of your previous work.

title: ANSWER A PUBLIC SCANDAL
text: {{rival}} has added a verse about you to a public performance. {{client}} offers a stage, with no guarantee that powerful listeners will laugh.

choices.label: Use facts and keep the verse measured

outcome.text: The verse stays close to facts that can be defended after the laughter.
Your public verse names the powerful subject and places your safety beside the rhyme.

choices.label: Test the verse with a fellow performer

outcome.text: A fellow performer tests the verse before it reaches the public stage.

title: DEFEND A TENANT
text: {{client}} needs evidence prepared for a proper hearing. An advocate’s opinion cannot erase a charge or end a lawful sentence.

choices.label: Prepare the real evidence for a hearing

outcome.text: Your evidence bundle is submitted for the hearing; the court retains judgment.
You publicly dispute the prosecution’s account without claiming a pardon.
A second advocate reviews the evidence and lawful grounds for defence.

title: INVESTIGATE A CHARTER
text: {{client}} produces an ancient charter whose youngest witness is inconveniently still alive. The ink and testimony need checking.

outcome.text: The charter is checked against its witnesses and surviving copies.

choices.label: Accuse the claimant of forgery now

outcome.text: You accuse the claimant openly before every disputed mark is explained.
A second reader compares the ink, names and boundaries.

title: HEAR A SWORN CASE
text: {{client}} brings a sworn boundary dispute. Both neighbours claim a pig which appears to prefer a third household.

choices.label: Record sworn testimony for the court

outcome.text: Sworn testimony is recorded for the judge to consider.
Your public opinion enters the dispute as advice, with the actual court still responsible.

choices.label: Seek an agreed submission to the judge

outcome.text: The neighbours receive a proposal for an agreed submission to the judge.

title: RECRUIT AN ASSOCIATE
text: {{client}} proposes joining your associates. Their account includes three debts and an unusually detailed knowledge of the sheriff’s route.

outcome.text: The proposed associate’s debts and account are checked before an agreement.

choices.label: Promise a large share for quick service

outcome.text: You offer a large share for quick service and take the risk of an untested promise.

choices.label: Ask a trusted associate to vouch for them

outcome.text: A trusted associate is asked to stake their reputation on the newcomer.

title: ORGANISE AN OPERATION
text: {{client}} brings a plan for a collector’s chest. The guards, escape route and division of the proceeds remain unsettled.

choices.label: Scout guards and plan an escape

outcome.text: The plan records guards, an escape route and what to do if the chest is empty.
You bring the operation forward to exploit the present guard’s weakness.

choices.label: Divide the operation among trusted partners

outcome.text: Partners receive separate roles and a witnessed division of the expected proceeds.

title: INVESTIGATE AN INFORMER
text: {{client}} suspects an informer. {{rival}} is repeating details that only a few associates were supposed to know.

outcome.text: The inquiry compares each leaked detail with the people who knew it.
You confront the suspected informer and risk warning the real source.

choices.label: Use an associate to check the story

outcome.text: An associate quietly checks the account against a second witness.

title: THE RENT NOTCH
text: Your guardian’s tally stick has one notch too many. The bailiff has brought a sack large enough to contain your supper.

outcome.text: The split tally proves the payment. Your household keeps its grain.
The fresh cut betrays you. Your fellow learner is accused of lending the knife.

choices.label: Ask the bailiff to produce his half

outcome.text: Your guardian brings both halves of the tally to the reeve. Neither can be altered without leaving a scar.

title: THE SEED POT
text: A rat has drowned in the pot of seed grain. Your cousin proposes burying the evidence in tomorrow’s bread.

outcome.text: You save enough clean seed for a strip of field and share the credit.
They are made to scrub the pot. They memorise your smile.

choices.label: Ask how seed should be stored

outcome.text: Your guardian shows you a dry bin with a stone lid. The lesson costs a pot, not a harvest.

title: LETTERS ON THE DOOR
text: Your guardian teaches letters on a soot-blackened door. A neighbour mistakes the alphabet for a curse.

outcome.text: The neighbour apologises to the letter B. Your guardian lets you keep the chalk.
The neighbour crosses himself at your classmate. Friendship grows colder.

choices.label: Ask your guardian to explain the letters

outcome.text: Your guardian reads a household name aloud. The neighbour recognises it and puts down the holy water.

title: THE WOOL ACCOUNT
text: The household owes six fleeces. A damp fleece weighs twice as much and smells like a drowned sheep.

outcome.text: The account balances before anyone reaches for a cudgel.

choices.label: Hide the damp one in a rival’s sack

outcome.text: The smell follows your rival into chapel. So does a grievance.

choices.label: Ask the wool buyer for a dry weight

outcome.text: The buyer provides a dry standard. Your guardian teaches you to record it before accepting a fleece.

title: THE SAINT WITH TWO ELBOWS
text: Your teacher asks you to copy the relic inventory. Saint Aelfric now possesses three elbows and no head.

outcome.text: You restore one elbow to its rightful saint. Your teacher praises your care.

choices.label: Let your classmate copy the error

outcome.text: The visiting canon questions your classmate before the whole parish.

choices.label: Ask the canon to inspect the relic roll

outcome.text: The canon compares the old roll with yours. Saint Aelfric loses an elbow without further injury.

title: THE PSALTER PIG
text: A pig eats the lower half of a psalter page. Your mentor suggests that Providence has abbreviated the lesson.

outcome.text: You and your classmate remember enough to rescue the psalm.

choices.label: Accuse your classmate of feeding it

outcome.text: The pig escapes punishment. Your classmate does not.

choices.label: Bring the damaged page to the priest

outcome.text: The priest borrows a second psalter. You learn how a missing passage is checked rather than invented.

title: THE BURIAL FEE
text: A widow’s husband appears twice in the burial ledger. She refuses to pay for the second funeral on sound theological grounds.

outcome.text: The widow keeps her pennies. Your teacher trusts you with the ledger.

choices.label: Copy your rival’s signature beneath it

outcome.text: The widow curses your rival by name. They learn why at vespers.

choices.label: Ask the priest to cancel the duplicate burial

outcome.text: Your teacher strikes the second entry and explains why a clean correction beats a clever excuse.

title: THE BELL ROPE EXAMINATION
text: Your classmate is suspended from the bell rope, clutching the only clean lesson sheet.

choices.label: Help them down and share it

outcome.text: You both pass, though the bell announces it to three parishes.

choices.label: Read the answers while they dangle

outcome.text: Your work is excellent. Your classmate’s opinion of you is precise.

choices.label: Fetch the teacher and a ladder

outcome.text: The teacher lowers your classmate safely. The lesson resumes beneath a very quiet bell.

title: THE MASTER’S PERFECT HORSESHOE
text: Your master offers the inspector a horseshoe you saw crack beneath the hammer. Your fellow apprentice has been ordered to carry it.

outcome.text: Your repair holds. The master’s reputation now rests on your hands.
The master docks their supper. They keep the cracked shoe as evidence.

choices.label: Show the crack to the inspector

outcome.text: The inspector refuses the shoe. Your master accepts the rebuke rather less gracefully than the inspection fee.

title: THE STOLEN GUILD SEAL
text: A customer wants the guild seal on pewter spoons. The master’s silver sample is locked away with his drinking money.

outcome.text: The spoons fail the assay. Your careful work earns the inspector’s attention.
A false mark reaches the guild court. Your rival begins collecting witnesses.

choices.label: Ask the master to order a public assay

outcome.text: Your master orders the assay in front of witnesses. You learn how a mark binds the maker to the metal.

title: THE APPRENTICE’S FINGER
text: A younger apprentice traps a finger in the vice. The commission is due before the bells.

outcome.text: The apprentice keeps the finger and helps finish your commission.

choices.label: Tell the master your rival tightened it

outcome.text: The vice is opened. Your rival’s prospects close a little.

choices.label: Call the master to open the vice

outcome.text: The master stops the job and releases the apprentice. You lose an hour and learn why a commission has no fingers.

title: THE MASTERPIECE IN THE ASHES
text: A spark lands on your measured drawing. Your rival’s drawing is excellent, and unattended.

outcome.text: Your teacher tests every line. The work is slow and yours.
The compass holes match their old work. Your mentor is less foolish than you hoped.

choices.label: Ask the master to check your surviving measurements

outcome.text: The master helps reconstruct the burnt drawing. Each borrowed measurement is acknowledged in the margin.

title: THE DEVIL IN THE MARGIN
text: Your classmate draws a bishop being swallowed by a snail. The dean calls for the artist.

choices.label: Defend it as a moral warning

outcome.text: The dean accepts a sermon on vanity. Your classmate owes you a kindness.
Your rival scrapes parchment for a week and starts a private list of sins.

choices.label: Ask the dean what the snail signifies

outcome.text: The dean invents an allegory with astonishing speed. Your mentor explains which parts can safely be repeated.

title: THE GREEK THAT WASN’T
text: Your mentor’s prized Greek quotation is a laundry account in a merchant’s cipher.

outcome.text: The master changes his lecture. You receive access to a better manuscript.
The chapter learns the price of washing six shirts. Your rival learns betrayal.

choices.label: Show the quotation to your teacher in private

outcome.text: Your teacher replaces the quotation before the lecture. You receive a lesson in translating before pontificating.

title: THE FASTING DISPUTATION
text: The chapter argues whether a goose is a fish while the cook holds the knife.

outcome.text: Your argument saves the goose until supper. Your teacher respects the scholarship.

choices.label: Attribute the heresy to your rival

outcome.text: Your rival must defend a goose they have never met.

choices.label: Ask the cook to suspend judgement

outcome.text: The cook postpones the knife while your mentor checks the authorities. Theology briefly becomes useful to a goose.

title: THE MEDICAL GLOSS
text: A manuscript recommends bloodletting after a faint. Your classmate has fainted directly beneath it.

outcome.text: You keep the lancet shut and fetch water. Your classmate recovers.
The mentor catches the forged hand before the lancet opens. The grudge remains real.

choices.label: Fetch the infirmarer before the lancet

outcome.text: The infirmarer orders water and rest. Your teacher makes you record the observation beside the disputed gloss.

title: THE PAGE AND THE PRIVY
text: Your first watch is outside the lord’s privy. A visitor insists the password is a matter of terrible urgency.

outcome.text: The visitor is admitted under escort. The sergeant trusts your judgement.

choices.label: Send your rival to stop him

outcome.text: Your rival receives the chamber pot and the blame.

choices.label: Ask the sergeant to take the watch

outcome.text: The sergeant handles the visitor and explains when urgency is an excuse and when it is a medical fact.

title: THE SQUIRE’S WOODEN HORSE
text: Your classmate’s practice saddle slips. The master calls this an opportunity to demonstrate courage.

outcome.text: Your classmate lands upright and later returns the favour.
The fall is noticed. So are your hands on the buckle.

choices.label: Ask the riding master to inspect the saddle

outcome.text: The master repairs the girth. You are made to inspect every buckle before the next ride.

title: THE BLUNT LANCE
text: The training lance bears a fresh split. The armourer offers to paint over it before the inspection.

outcome.text: You lose an afternoon and save a face. Your master credits the inspection.

choices.label: Put it in your rival’s rack

outcome.text: The shaft breaks in their hands. They remember who visited the rack.

choices.label: Bring the shaft to the armourer

outcome.text: The armourer replaces the split wood and teaches you where a painted crack will still show under pressure.

title: THE HUNGRY MUSTER
text: The muster roll includes four dead soldiers and a horse listed as a cousin.

outcome.text: Rations reach the actual company. Your teacher praises useful arithmetic.

choices.label: Sign your rival’s name to it

outcome.text: Your rival answers to the captain for a horse’s family tree.

choices.label: Ask the quartermaster to recount the roll

outcome.text: The quartermaster removes four ghosts and one horse. Your tutor makes you copy the corrected ration order.

title: THE WRONG COAT OF ARMS
text: Your tutor asks you to seat two cousins whose fathers died fighting over the same painted badger.

outcome.text: You separate the cousins by three bishops. Dinner survives.

choices.label: Give your rival the seating plan

outcome.text: They face two angry households. Your tutor identifies the handwriting.

choices.label: Ask the herald to verify the disputed arms

outcome.text: The herald seats both cousins far from sharp cutlery. Your tutor explains the disputed descent.

title: THE ACCOUNT OF THE SWANS
text: The steward counts twelve swans. The kitchen accounts for thirteen swan pies.

outcome.text: The thirteenth bird was a goose. Your tutor commends the audit.

choices.label: Charge the missing bird to your rival

outcome.text: The steward demands payment. Your rival begins auditing you.

choices.label: Ask the steward to reconcile the kitchen roll

outcome.text: The steward finds the goose receipt. You learn to audit the purchases before accusing the cook.

title: THE EMBASSY’S CHAIRS
text: An envoy’s chair is an inch lower than yours. His secretary calls it an insult to the whole coast.

outcome.text: Everyone suffers equally. Your tutor calls this diplomacy.

choices.label: Say your rival ordered the chairs

outcome.text: The envoy records your rival’s name beside the word grievance.

choices.label: Ask the chamberlain to change every seat

outcome.text: The chamberlain replaces the chairs. Your tutor notes that equal discomfort is a workable diplomatic settlement.

title: THE TENANT’S PETITION
text: A tenant petitions for seed. Your tutor says this is an exercise in household administration. The tenant says he is an exercise in starvation.

choices.label: Check the granary and draft relief

outcome.text: The lesson becomes a workable petition. Your classmate helps calculate it.
The tenant curses your rival. Your tutor catches the borrowed seal.

choices.label: Ask the tutor to examine the seed petition

outcome.text: Your tutor measures the household’s need against the stores. The petitioner receives an answer based on grain rather than manners.

title: THE WINTER ACCOUNT
text: {{mentor}} brings your household ledger. Winter grain and a creditor fall due together.

outcome.text: The plan protects seed and supper.

choices.label: Hide the arrears in the seed account

outcome.text: Your colleague finds the missing debt beside their signature.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to review the winter stores

outcome.text: Your tutor separates the seed reserve from the debt payment and sets a practical accounting exercise.

title: AN EVENING OF LETTERS
text: After work, {{classmate}} asks you to read a tenancy clause neither of you understood as children.

choices.label: Read it against the old agreement

outcome.text: Your shared study finds the changed rent.
Your colleague carries your interpretation to the landlord.

choices.label: Read the disputed tenancy clause with {{mentor}}

outcome.text: Your tutor compares both agreements and asks you to explain each changed obligation.

title: THE LATE READER
text: {{mentor}} reserves an evening for adults learning their letters. {{classmate}} brings a contract rather than a psalter.

outcome.text: You separate the obligations from the ornament.
The copied hand wins praise that belongs to someone else.

choices.label: Ask for an evening reading exercise

outcome.text: Your teacher sets a short contract passage that can be studied after paid work.

title: A LETTER HOME
text: {{classmate}} needs a letter to a relative who has left for work. The parish desk is finally quiet.

outcome.text: Your colleague entrusts you with the reply.

choices.label: Read the private lines aloud for a laugh

outcome.text: The laughter travels; so does the betrayal.

choices.label: Ask how to write a private reply

outcome.text: Your teacher helps form a respectful letter while preserving your colleague’s confidence.

title: THE LATE APPRENTICE
text: An older apprentice is assigned the heaviest work. {{mentor}} asks whether your previous experience changes the arrangement.

choices.label: Propose a trial piece and fair rotation

outcome.text: Your work earns an adult place at the bench.

choices.label: Claim {{classmate}} made the flawed trial piece

outcome.text: The commission carries an innocent maker’s mark.

choices.label: Ask for an assessment of your previous craft work

outcome.text: Your master tests your existing skills and records what the late apprenticeship still requires.

title: THE EVENING MASTERPIECE
text: Your paying work leaves one evening to finish the apprenticeship sample. {{classmate}} offers measurements.

choices.label: Credit their help and submit your own work

outcome.text: The master tests the work and acknowledges both hands.

choices.label: Submit their sample under your mark

outcome.text: Your colleague keeps the original drawing.
The master checks the surviving measurements and sets a smaller, honest trial piece.

title: THE INFERMARER’S COMMENTARY
text: {{mentor}} asks your adult seminar to compare a fever diary with an old authority. The patient’s actual course contradicts the gloss.

outcome.text: The seminar adopts a more careful account of care.

choices.label: Alter the diary to flatter the authority

outcome.text: Your colleague retains the unaltered observations.
Your teacher asks you to distinguish an observed symptom from an authority’s assumption.

title: THE VISITING EXAMINER
text: A visiting examiner asks how your learning was acquired while you worked. {{mentor}} can certify the hours actually completed.

outcome.text: Your remaining requirements are written clearly.
The borrowed certificate passes today. A later review may compare the signatures.

choices.label: Ask for the actual examination requirements

outcome.text: The examiner writes down the hours and arguments still required for a legitimate certificate.

title: THE VETERAN AT DRILL
text: {{classmate}} has seen a siege; you are learning formations after years in another trade. {{mentor}} asks for a plan.

choices.label: Combine practical experience with the drill

outcome.text: The exercise gives both adult learners useful work.

choices.label: Claim their campaign experience as yours

outcome.text: The sergeant begins asking which company remembers you.

choices.label: Review the drill with the veteran and {{mentor}}

outcome.text: Your trainer sets an exercise that tests the veteran’s experience and your understanding together.

title: THE CONTRACTED WATCH
text: Your training company must cover a night watch while keeping time for its adult recruits’ paid work.

outcome.text: The company trusts the rota because you serve it too.

choices.label: Put your colleague on every cold watch

outcome.text: The rota is copied, along with its author’s name.

choices.label: Ask the captain to review the watch rotation

outcome.text: The captain checks the recruits’ paid work and makes you explain a fair allocation of cold watches.

title: THE PRIVATE TUTOR’S TABLE
text: {{mentor}} teaches court practice to adults. {{classmate}} brings a petition from their own household.

choices.label: Draft advice from the actual accounts

outcome.text: Your tutor commends a useful answer rather than a fine bow.

choices.label: Trade their private grievance for influence

outcome.text: The petition returns to its author with your name attached.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to examine the household petition

outcome.text: The tutor checks the figures and asks you to justify each proposed relief payment.

title: THE ADULT AUDIENCE
text: An envoy questions why your household can afford tutoring while tenants petition for seed.

choices.label: Explain the accounts and propose affordable relief

outcome.text: Your reasoning survives questions from your colleague.
The document opens a door. The seal may be checked later.

choices.label: Ask for a witnessed court examination

outcome.text: Your tutor offers a legitimate assessment instead of a borrowed seal; the remaining preparation is recorded.

title: THE ROUT
text: The lines dissolve into screaming chaos. A mounted knight in enemy colours bears down on you, lance lowered. There is no time to think.

success.text: You set your spear and the charging horse impaled itself. You stand, blood-soaked and alive, a hero of the field. The lord himself learns your name.

failure.text: The lance took you in the shoulder and the world went white. You wake days later in a surgeon’s tent, ruined but breathing.

choices.label: Dive into the mud and play dead

success.text: You lay among the fallen, unmoving, until the horses thundered past. Survival has no honour, but it has a pulse.

failure.text: A looter found you "dead" and was most surprised when you flinched. The scuffle did not go your way.

effects.death: Cut down by a battlefield looter while feigning death.

outcome.text: As a knight, you are worth more alive. You yield your sword and are held for ransom, which is humiliating and survivable, in that order.

title: THE COMMON HEDGE
text: {{other.name}} moves a boundary hedge while you organise the village work. By dusk two households are shouting over a strip of common ground and everyone expects you to decide whether this was theft or a mistake.

outcome.text: You find the old stones beneath the nettles and put the hedge back where memory and mud agree it belongs.
You declare the moved hedge reasonable. {{other.name}} remembers the loyalty; the other household remembers everything else.
The reeve restores the boundary, fines both households for wasting his morning, and thanks you by assigning next month’s ditch work.

title: THE MASTERS’ PRICE
text: {{other.name}} closes the guild-room door and lays out a simple proposal: every workshop will raise its prices together, and anyone who refuses will find supplies strangely unavailable.

outcome.text: You keep your prices honest. Customers crowd your door, while three suppliers suddenly forget the road to your workshop.
The new prices hold. Your purse grows heavier and the poorest customers begin repairing old things instead of buying yours.
You secure one price for noble orders and another for neighbours who arrive with mended sleeves. Nobody loves it, which is how you know it is a bargain.

title: WHAT WAS SAID IN DARKNESS
text: The voice behind the screen is {{other.name}}’s. The confession concerns a plan that may hurt innocent people, but repeating it would break the seal that made the truth possible.

outcome.text: You say nothing. {{other.name}} leaves knowing the secret is safe, while you spend the night wondering who may pay for that safety.

choices.label: Warn the threatened household
choices.hint: Prevent harm without naming the source

outcome.text: You deliver a warning wrapped in enough scripture to conceal its origin. The household prepares, and {{other.name}} watches you more carefully afterward.
You name the danger and its source. The plan dies immediately, along with every honest confession likely to reach you for years.

title: THE FORBIDDEN GLOSS
text: {{other.name}} recognises the hand in a censored margin: a respected scholar condemned years ago. The erased argument is persuasive, useful, and dangerous to possess.

outcome.text: You hide the argument inside an innocent commentary where a careful reader may recover it. Knowledge survives by learning to whisper.

memory.note: You preserved a forbidden argument inside an innocent manuscript.

choices.label: Finish the erasure
choices.hint: Protect the house; destroy the passage

outcome.text: Fresh scraping removes the last readable words. The manuscript is safe, the scriptorium is safe, and the thought exists only in your memory.
The prior reads the passage twice, locks the book away, and orders that no punishment follow. Half the house calls that mercy and half calls it fear.

title: ONE SPEAR MISSING
text: At roll call {{other.name}} is absent. You find them behind the tithe barn, shaking, with a widowed parent at home and no intention of marching toward a war they do not understand.

outcome.text: A fever appears in the roll beside {{other.name}}’s name. Their household keeps its last able pair of hands and your captain begins counting more carefully.
You promise to place them in the rear rank and bring them home if promises survive battle. They return because you asked, not because the levy did.
{{other.name}} is bound before the whole levy. Nobody else deserts, and nobody meets your eye during the march.

title: TWO CLAIMS, ONE MEADOW
text: {{other.name}} arrives with a charter, while another household arrives with three generations of grazing and no parchment at all. Both claims are convincing. The meadow is not large enough to satisfy either.

outcome.text: The grazing continues as it always has. {{other.name}} folds the charter very carefully and begins asking who else doubts written law.
The seal wins. The meadow changes hands before sunset, and an old household begins selling the animals it can no longer graze.
You mark alternate grazing weeks. Both sides call it impossible and both follow the schedule once they think nobody is watching.

title: THE EMPTY GRANARIES
text: The council’s figures agree on one fact: there is not enough grain for the army, the towns, and the winter poor. {{other.name}} asks which promise should be broken first.

outcome.text: Army stores are opened at the church doors. The hungry eat, the captains protest, and every mother in the queue learns whose order did it.
The military granaries remain sealed. The levy will march well-fed past villages that are not.
Merchants empty your treasury and fill the quays. It is an undignified solution to hunger, which remains preferable to a dignified famine.

title: THE MISSING SHARE
text: The gang’s purse is light by twelve gold. {{other.name}} had the key, denies taking it, and offers three different explanations before anyone asks for one.

outcome.text: You find six gold beneath a floorboard and accept that the other six purchased silence. The gang survives with a new lock and an old suspicion.
{{other.name}} leaves without the purse and with every name, route, and hiding place the gang has used this year.
You name the theft, forgive it, and make {{other.name}} earn the money back beside you. Half the gang calls it weakness; the other half would now follow you anywhere.

title: THE WRONG SEAT
text: Before the first loaf is cut, {{other.name}} objects to where you have seated them. The complaint is supposedly about precedence and unmistakably about an insult from twelve years ago.

outcome.text: Benches scrape, children carry trenchers, and everyone moves one place. The ancient insult survives but tonight’s supper does too.

choices.label: Give {{other.name}} the high seat
choices.hint: Win one ally; slight the rest

outcome.text: {{other.name}} receives the high seat and becomes gracious at once. Three other guests become historians.

success.text: You retell the old insult until even its victim laughs. By pudding, the rival households are correcting your version together.

failure.text: Your joke lands like a brick in a baptismal font. {{other.name}} leaves before supper and takes two cousins with them.

title: THE PARISH HEARS A NAME
text: Your sermon against hidden sin is still echoing when someone in the nave points at {{other.name}}. The congregation turns as one body and waits for you to confirm an accusation you never made.

outcome.text: You turn the next half-hour toward mercy until pointing fingers lower. {{other.name}} remains shaken, but the parish leaves with nobody to punish.
You do not speak the name, but you do not deny it. By evening {{other.name}}’s door bears a mark in chalk and the collection plate is unusually heavy.

choices.label: Admit the sermon went too far

outcome.text: You say plainly that zeal outran wisdom. A few parishioners sneer, more look relieved, and {{other.name}} stays to help extinguish the candles.

title: JUDGMENT BEFORE SWINEFORD
text: state=>{const legal=state.world.characters[state.playerCharacterId]?.legalState;const charge=legal?.charges.find(item=>!item.resolved);return`The reeve reads the charge of ${charge?.offence??"an offence against local law"}. Evidence, reputation and old enemies now carry as much weight as truth.`}

success.text: Your defence exposes enough doubt for the charge to fail.

failure.text: The court rejects your defence and orders imprisonment.

outcome.text: Your confession shortens the hearing, though not the memory of it.

success.text: Coin changes a witness’s certainty, and the charge collapses.

failure.text: The bribe is exposed before the court. The new charge proves easier than the old one.
